fragments.text: An installation has one initial owner claim, invited staff, email-link return and revocable sessions.
Development personas are separately gated and confer no production authority.
The initial claim is a setup step, not a single point of failure: several admins, delegated admin roles and owner transfer are ADMIN-003, and enforced multi-factor sign-in is ADMIN-004.
**Acceptance evidence:** Through setup, invitation, sign-in and the library API, reject a second claim, revoke a live session, deactivate/reactivate staff and prove prior sessions stay invalid.
Exercise owner and reviewer in the built browser journey.
Owners manage collections, editable typed schemas, required fields, accountable people and groups.
Schema edits preserve authoritative stored values, diagnose missing/invalid fields only on accessible records, and validate new filings and uploads against current definitions.
**Acceptance evidence:** Create and edit a type through the owner form/API; preserve an old record unchanged while diagnosing it, reject invalid new values and hide diagnostics from an outsider.
Uploads validate actual bytes, SHA-256 and size.
Durable original-object custody precedes atomic record admission; invalid or failed uploads never appear as successful library files.

**Acceptance evidence:** Upload an original through the document API, compare its retained hash/size and download bytes, and submit bad checksum, size and filing values without creating a visible record.
Supplier, customer and project filing retains original names, typed values and responsibility.
Moves require current source-record and destination-collection editor access; inherited access follows the destination while versions and review history remain intact.

**Acceptance evidence:** Move a reviewed file through the filing API between differently shared collections; reject a source-only editor, then prove new readers gain access and former readers lose search/download access without changed versions.
Signature-classified PDF/raster and escaped UTF-8 text can be previewed.
Unknown formats remain downloadable; active HTML/SVG is sandboxed plain text.
Broader rendering is PREVIEW-001.
**Acceptance evidence:** Open text, PDF and raster previews from the built document page at 1440 and 390; download an unknown original, and verify sandbox/no-store/nosniff headers and inactive SVG.
Current access filters lists, counts, title/metadata/admitted-text search, detail, preview, download and mutations.
Derived text records parser provenance and exact version identity; it never creates access of its own.

**Acceptance evidence:** Search distinctive admitted text as owner, reviewer and outsider, then revoke a group grant and repeat list/count/detail/preview/download/mutation requests, including old version URLs.
Every replacement is a new immutable original.
For a governed file, approved A remains current while B/C await review; approving B never selects pending C.
Ordinary file editing also retains history without requiring a review workflow (SPACE-001).
Browsing, naming and restoring earlier versions as current by every contributor and editor is VERSION-001; restoring on a governed file never moves the approved pointer without approval.
**Acceptance evidence:** Upload A, B and C through the versions API, approve B explicitly and download each original, proving the approved pointer and earlier bytes never silently change.
Assignment, comments, requested changes and approval record actor and version.
Assignment grants no access.
Requested changes require a new immutable submission; only the assigned reviewer with current reviewer access can approve it.

**Acceptance evidence:** Request changes, reject approval of the rejected version and an unassigned actor, submit corrected bytes, and approve that exact version while preserving prior events and the earlier approved pointer until approval.
Separate review and expiry dates create due/upcoming work.
Completion records its actor, date and investigation evidence without destroying the file or treating an expiry as a deletion instruction.
Automated follow-up is FOLLOW-001.
**Acceptance evidence:** Create both dates, inspect the work list, reject an empty completion and complete only review with evidence; expiry and originals remain.
The owner grants/revokes reader, editor and reviewer access for people/groups.
Effective readers need active local identities; current group membership governs access, and imported people alone have no authentication authority.
The full five-level space role model, delegated granting by space managers and policy-bound sharing by editors are ROLE-001 and SHARE-004; these grant rules continue to hold under them.

**Acceptance evidence:** Grant a group, inspect effective readers, remove its member and revoke collection access through the API; prove denial of details, search, previews, downloads and review mutations.
Archive preview writes no documents and lists every item, hash, duplicate, mapping and gap.
Apply binds the reviewed fingerprint and current authority;
Base D1 journal/native target publish inert records, resume after restart and undo only untouched batches.
Unsafe paths or corrupt bytes publish no documents.

**Acceptance evidence:** Preview/apply a bounded archive through the archive API, reject changed fingerprint/traversal/corruption, restart and resume, undo untouched records and preserve a conflicting native edit.
Source decisions never become new Chest approvals.

Local RER export and empty-target restore retain the semantic graph, portable people/groups/roles/grants, all original version bytes, derived provenance, decisions, completions, trash, audit and import custody.
Credentials and dispatch outbox are excluded; setup regenerates secrets and old credentials fail.
Nonempty/corrupt restore is atomic refusal.
Private archives cannot be exported into served assets and archive-bearing public assets block build/setup.

**Acceptance evidence:** Use real RER export/import in a fresh target, compare all portable cells and original chunks, reject corrupt/nonempty/tampered metadata restores and public-asset exposure, then sign in afresh and recheck private imported records and trash.
Every user has a trash view of the items they trashed and restores any of them, files or whole folder trees, with no owner or admin involved, provided they still hold the role that let them trash it.
Space managers and content managers (ROLE-001) see and restore every trashed item in their space whoever trashed it; admins with content-recovery scope (ADMIN-003) restore across spaces.
Viewers, commenters and contributors cannot trash shared-space items and cannot restore someone else's.
A restored folder returns with its tree, versions, stable IDs, comments and inherited permissions; restoring never re-enables a revoked link or identity.
Trash retains originals and history indefinitely until a separately authorized erasure; no age or expiry silently destroys them.

Permanent removal from trash belongs only to space managers and admins under ERASE-001 for shared-space items, and to the owning user for items in their own personal area; trashed bytes keep counting towards storage limits until erased (QUOTA-001).
Mutations are audited, and current access filters activity views.
Point-in-time folder and personal-area rewind is RECOVER-001; admin account rewind is ADMIN-003.

**Acceptance evidence:** Through the API and browser at 1440 and 390, a staff editor trashes a nested folder of their own in a team space and restores it from their own trash view, tree, hashes, version IDs and stable links identical, with no owner session involved.

A space reader is refused restore (403) of that folder and a contributor is refused trash; a space manager restores an item another member trashed; a manager's permanent-delete request goes through ERASE-001 while an editor's is refused.
The trashed item disappears from a reviewer's list/search/download, and each trash/restore appears once in the audit with actor and outcome.
The owner creates a team space and nested folders inside it (for example Clients › Harbor Freight › Contracts), shown with a breadcrumb, and uploads files into any folder with the file picker.
On a phone-width screen the folder page also offers **Take a photo**, which opens the camera picker and uploads the photo into that folder.

**Acceptance evidence:** Create a team space and two nested folders in the browser, upload a PDF and a text file into the innermost folder, and at 390 pixels upload an image through **Take a photo**; each file opens on its own page inside the breadcrumb.
A large file goes up in parts with its progress shown.

If the page is reloaded or the connection drops, the folder lists it under **Unfinished uploads** with the share already received; choosing the same file again continues from the parts already stored instead of starting over.
The finished file's stored SHA-256 and downloaded bytes equal the original.

**Acceptance evidence:** Upload a 150 MB file, reload the page once progress passes a quarter, see "Unfinished uploads · N% of 150.0 MB received", choose the same file again, see progress resume above zero, and compare the stored and downloaded SHA-256 with the original's.
Each upload of a new version is kept in the file's version history with its number, author, time, size and SHA-256.
**Restore as current version** on an earlier version adds a new version marked "restore of version N" whose bytes equal that version; the later versions stay in the history.

**Acceptance evidence:** Upload three versions of a file, restore version 1, and check that version 4 reads "restore of version 1", its downloaded bytes equal version 1, and versions 1 to 3 are still listed.

**Restore to a date** on a folder takes a date and time with its time zone and first shows a preview listing each change it would make (a renamed file renamed back, a trashed file brought back, a file added since moved to trash).
Nothing changes until **Restore selected items**.
The receipt offers **Undo this restore**, which returns the folder to how it was just before the restore.

**Acceptance evidence:** Note a minute, then rename one file, trash another and add a third in a folder; preview a restore to that minute and see the three changes with the folder unchanged; apply it and see the folder's contents as they were; undo it and see the renamed, trashed and added state again.
A file's **Link for anyone** can carry a password (8 characters or more), an expiry date and a download limit, and its row shows "Expires … · N of M downloads".
Someone without an account who opens it is asked for the password; a wrong password is refused.
Once the limit is used, the link shows "Download limit reached".
**Revoke** turns a link off at once: it then shows "Link turned off".

**Acceptance evidence:** Create a link with a password, tomorrow's expiry and a limit of 2; in a browser with no account, a wrong password is refused, the right one opens the file, two downloads succeed and the next visit shows "Download limit reached".
Create a second link, open it, revoke it, and see "Link turned off".
**Links › Shared too widely** lists items with a link anyone can open without signing in that never expires, or one past its expiry or download limit, with the reason.
**Make private** on such an item turns off every link on it; the item leaves the list and its links stop opening.

**Acceptance evidence:** Create a link for anyone with no expiry on a folder, see the folder under Shared too widely with "Never expires", press Make private, and see it leave the list and the link stop opening.
A folder's **File request** gives a link that someone with no account opens to upload files into that folder, with their name and email if they give them.
The upload lands in the folder, and on a hosted Chest the person who made the request is emailed "New files from your file request" naming the uploader, the file and the folder.

**Acceptance evidence:** Create a file request on a folder, open its link in a browser with no account, upload a PDF with a name and email, see "Files received", find the file in the folder, and on a hosted Chest receive the notice email.
Search finds files by words inside their PDF text, including files that arrived through a file request.
It shows only files the searcher can open: words inside a file in a space they are not a member of are not found.

**Acceptance evidence:** Search a word that appears only inside an uploaded PDF and inside a PDF received through a file request, and find both; as a member outside a space, search a word inside one of its files and find nothing, while the owner's same search finds it.
A person added to a team space as a viewer sees that space and opens its folders and files, but has no upload, new folder, share, rename or trash action, and the server refuses those actions (403).
A file in a space they are not in shows **Request access** without its name, and People & settings is refused (403).

**Acceptance evidence:** Add a second person to a space as viewer; as them, check the actions are absent and a rename request is refused with 403, open a file of another space and see Request access with no name, and open People & settings and get 403.
`rer deploy` puts Chest on the owner's Cloudflare account (a Worker, a D1 database and an R2 bucket) with the owner's own mail provider (the gate used SendGrid).
People sign in by an emailed link, and invited people get an invitation email.
`rer run hosted-backup` saves the hosted database and every original into a private folder;

`rer run hosted-restore` puts them into a freshly deployed Chest, after which the owner and invited people sign in by email again and find their spaces, folders, files, versions, links, file requests, trash and grants.
`rer deploy --remove --yes` deletes the Worker, database and bucket and reads back that none remains.

**Acceptance evidence:** Deploy, sign in as the owner by email, invite a second person who accepts from the email, and use the jobs above; back up and check the backup holds data made only on the hosted Chest; remove, redeploy and restore; sign in again as both people by email and read back the folders, the trashed file with its versions, the link's download count, the file request and the 150 MB original byte for byte; remove and find no Worker, database or bucket left.

A Chest 0.1.0 copy moved to 0.2.0 in place (check out the new release, `rer install`, `rer dev`) applies migrations 0016 to 0020, which only add tables, and keeps every earlier database row and stored original unchanged.
Its Library documents open with every version's bytes, its people stay, and Files works.

**Acceptance evidence:** Install 0.1.0, add people, a collection, a document type and two documents with two versions each, snapshot every table and stored object, upgrade in place, and check every earlier row and object is unchanged, every version downloads with its SHA-256, and a team space can be created.

Staff store everyday files in personal areas and team-owned hierarchical shared folders, create/rename/move/copy folders and mixed Office/PDF/Google content, create new documents, spreadsheets and presentations from blank or a template in any folder (EDIT-004), star/recently open files and transfer content ownership when staff leave.

Outside offboarding, a user can hand ownership of a single file or folder in their personal area to a colleague: the colleague gets an in-app and email request and accepts or declines; until acceptance the sender stays owner, and on acceptance the item moves to the recipient's personal area with its stable ID, versions, links and grants intact and the sender kept as editor unless they choose otherwise.
Stable IDs survive moves.
Ordinary upload/edit/open works without mandatory schema, reviewer or approval; owners opt selected folders into CHEST-02/07/08 governance.
Space managers set membership and inherited/restricted subfolder roles from the ROLE-001 levels with an effective-access explanation.
Each space serves at least the SCALE-001 reference size (500,000 items, 100 nested folder levels, 600 direct members) without changed behavior.
fragments.note: the sentence restated the scale reference size; reference sizes live only in SCALE-001.1

fragments.text: Who may create a space, and the settings a new space starts with, are SPACE-002.
fragments.note: duplicate: a cross-reference to SPACE-002, which states who creates spaces and the settings new spaces start with

fragments.text: **Acceptance evidence:** As two staff and an admin, build a nested project tree, upload an ordinary file with no review configuration, edit/move it, restrict a subfolder and offboard its creator; the team retains content and stable links while the former user is denied.

A staff member offers ownership of a personal-area file to a colleague: before acceptance the sender is still owner; after acceptance the file sits in the recipient's area with the same stable ID, versions and share link, the sender is editor, and a declined offer changes nothing; each step is audited.
Repeat browser navigation at 1440 and 390, then repeat listing, move and restriction in a space loaded to the SCALE-001 reference size and record the SCALE-001 timings.
Admins with service-settings scope (ADMIN-003) choose who may create team spaces:
**everyone**, **named groups only** or **admins only**.
A user who may not create one sees no create action, is refused with the rule named in the UI and API, and can send a space request that reaches admins with that scope and is audited.

Admins also set the **defaults for new spaces**, organization-wide with overrides per creator group: whether people outside the organization may be given access (POLICY-001 external sharing for the space); whether people who are not space members may be added to its files and folders; whether content managers may share folders, not only files; whether viewers and commenters may download, print and copy (the ROLE-001 no-download setting); the space's default link audience (SHARE-001/POLICY-001); and its starting storage limit (QUOTA-001).
A further default, **allow space managers to override these settings**, decides whether a manager may change any defaulted setting in their own space.
With it off, a manager's change to a defaulted setting is refused with the rule named in the UI and API, while admins can still change it per space.
Defaults apply only to spaces created after the change; existing spaces keep their current settings, and the console says so before saving.
Organization POLICY-001 restrictions still win over any space setting.
Every change to the creation rule, a default or the override switch is audited with before and after values.
**Acceptance evidence:** Limit space creation to the group "Ops leads".
A staff member outside it sees no create action, and a direct form post and an API call are each refused with the rule named; their space request reaches an admin.
A group member creates a space.

Set the defaults to external access off, non-member file access off, viewer and commenter download off and manager override off, then create a new space: it starts with those settings, and a space created earlier is unchanged.
That space's manager tries to turn external access on through the UI and the API and is refused with the rule named; an admin changes it successfully.
Turn manager override on and see the manager's change succeed.
Inspect the audit with before and after values.
Run the browser steps at 1440 and 390.
Spaces, folders and files grant one of five cumulative roles to people, groups and guests (SHARE-005):
**viewer** (open, preview, see version history, download unless restricted, and open office files read-only in the EDIT-001 editor);

**commenter** (viewer plus comment, mention, assign comments and annotate under EDIT-003, and suggest edits in an EDIT-001 comment-and-suggest session, recorded as tracked changes in documents and never as direct edits);
**contributor** (add files and new versions, name versions and restore an earlier version as current under VERSION-001, edit content, and accept or reject suggestions, but not move, trash or share);
**content manager** (contributor plus move, copy out, trash/restore and share items within policy);
**manager** (content manager plus membership and role changes, permanent delete under ERASE-001, space settings and deleting the space).
The CHEST-10 reviewer duty is an attribute that combines with any level from commenter up and never implies more access.
File-level grants on personal-area items use viewer, commenter and editor (editor = contributor plus move/trash/share of that item).
Editors and content managers share items to people and groups when POLICY-001 allows it, and a manager can switch editor sharing off per space.

A per-space and per-file setting stops viewers and commenters from downloading, printing and copying; previews then stream rendered pages only and every original door (download, range, sync, API, archive, link) refuses them.
Role changes take effect on the next request through every door.

**Acceptance evidence:** For each role, one public-door test through the HTTP API and one through the browser UI attempts open, download, comment, open in the editor, suggest a change, accept a suggestion, view version history, upload a new version, restore an earlier version, move, copy out, trash, restore, share and change membership on a space folder and a file; each permitted action succeeds and each other is refused with 403 and no state change.

Turn on the no-download setting and prove viewer and commenter downloads, range requests, archive inclusion (BULK-001), sync hydration and API reads of the original are refused while pages still preview.
Switch editor sharing off and prove an editor's share is refused while a manager's succeeds.

In the EDIT-001 editor, the commenter's DOCX session records their typing as tracked changes attributed to them and a save carrying a direct edit is refused with `suggest_only`; the viewer's session is read-only and its save is refused; a contributor accepts the commenter's suggestion as an attributed version.
Downgrade a role mid-session and prove the next request uses the new role.

Every file has a version history listing each retained version with its author, time, size, SHA-256, how it arrived (upload, sync client, editor save, restore, migration or signature) and an optional name.

Anyone with viewer access or above sees the history, and anyone allowed to download the file downloads any retained version; the ROLE-001 no-download setting refuses older versions as it does the current one.
**Contributors, content managers and managers** on a space item, and **file editors** on a personal-area item can:
restore any retained version as the current one;
upload a replacement as the current version;
name and rename versions.
Viewers and commenters are refused all three.
A restore creates a new attributed version whose bytes equal the chosen version.
It never deletes or rewrites later versions, and it keeps the file's stable ID, links, grants and comment threads, so existing links serve the restored content.
Versions are retained indefinitely until a separately authorized erasure (CHEST-07, ERASE-001), so no version silently ages out.
On a governed file (CHEST-07/08) the restored version enters as a new submission awaiting review, and the approved pointer moves only by approval.
Restores reach open EDIT-001 sessions as a remote change.
Each restore, upload and rename is audited and shown in the file's activity.
Restoring many files or a whole folder to a point in time is RECOVER-001, and incident-wide restore is SECURITY-003.
Guest version operations:
SHARE-005; sync clients receiving restores:
SYNC-001.
**Acceptance evidence:** In a team space, staff A uploads an XLSX as version 1 and edits it to version 2; colleague B replaces it with version 3.
Through the API and the browser at 1440 and 390, contributor C opens the version history and sees the author, time and size of each version.
C downloads version 2 and checks its SHA-256, names it "Before Q3 edits" and restores it.
Version 4 is created by C with bytes equal to version 2; versions 1, 2 and 3 remain downloadable; the stable ID and an existing share link are unchanged and now serve version 4.
A viewer and a commenter see the history and download version 1, but their restore and rename are refused with 403 and no new version.
With the no-download setting on, the viewer's download of version 1 is refused.
On a governed file whose version 2 is approved, a restore of version 1 enters as a new submitted version while the approved pointer stays on version 2 until approval.
The audit records each restore once with actor and source version.
Browser, desktop and mobile upload whole folder trees and multi-GB originals with durable progress, pause/cancel/resume and per-item results.
The maximum single file is **5 TB** (5,000,000,000,000 bytes) through the desktop client, mobile app, public API and resumable browser upload; one folder upload accepts at least 100,000 items.
Resumption survives network/process loss, verifies bytes before publication and never duplicates a completed file.
Invalid names, case collisions, path lengths, QUOTA-001 storage limits, files above 5 TB and unsupported files have actionable item-level errors without losing other successes.

**Acceptance evidence:** Upload a nested folder containing a 50 GB video and duplicate names, interrupt connectivity and restart the client, then resume and compare hashes/tree/counts; cancel another transfer and prove no false success or half-visible file.
Through the public API, upload a 5 TB sparse-pattern test object with resumable parts and verify its SHA-256; a 5 TB + 1 byte declaration is refused before any bytes are stored.
Upload a 100,000-item folder and reconcile the per-item results.
Test a QUOTA-001 storage-limit refusal and retain completed files.

In the browser at 1440 and 390 and in the iOS and Android apps, the upload panel shows each file's percentage of bytes received and verified (for example "Uploading 62%"); reload the page or kill the app mid-upload and see the same file resume from its stored percentage, not from zero.

In the browser, desktop client and mobile app, users multi-select files and folders, including across subfolders and search results, and move, copy, share, trash, restore or download them in one action.
Each item is checked against the actor's current role (ROLE-001) and POLICY-001; refused items are reported per item without blocking the rest, and a partial result is never shown as complete.

Downloading a folder or selection streams one ZIP archive (ZIP64 for archives over 4 GB, original names and folder tree preserved) containing only items the actor may download, with a manifest listing each path, version ID, size and SHA-256 and each excluded item with its reason.
Guests on a folder link (SHARE-001/005) and request recipients get the same archive download within their grant.
Bulk operations are durable jobs that survive restart and are audited once per item.

**Acceptance evidence:** Multi-select 200 files across two subfolders, including 5 the actor may not download under a no-download setting, and download one archive in the browser at 1440 and on the mobile app; unzip it and reconcile tree, names and SHA-256 hashes against the manifest, with the 5 listed as excluded and absent.
Bulk-move and bulk-share the same selection where 3 items are refused by role or policy and see 197 successes plus 3 per-item refusals.
Restart the server mid-job and see it complete once without duplicate moves or audit entries.
Download a 6 GB folder as a guest through a folder link and verify the ZIP64 archive.
Signed, installable macOS and Windows clients mount Chest in Finder/Explorer for existing applications.
Users choose on-demand virtual files or mirrored folders per space; selective offline pinning, local cache budgets and visible hydration state let them open/save/rename/move files as local files.

On-demand files take no local disk space for their content until opened: each shows its name, size and state, opening one downloads only that file, and **Free up space** returns a downloaded file to online-only while it stays in place.
A restore under VERSION-001 reaches each signed-in client as a remote change to the same file, with the restored bytes and new version ID.
Client updates, sign-out and uninstall preserve unsent work and expose what remains locally.
Supported matrix:

**macOS 13 Ventura or later on Apple silicon (arm64) and Intel (x86_64)** through Apple's File Provider framework, and **Windows 10 22H2 and Windows 11 23H2 or later on x64 and ARM64** through the Windows Cloud Files API; each new major OS release joins the matrix within 90 days of general availability.
Installers are signed and notarized (Apple Developer ID) or Authenticode-signed, and deploy silently through MDM (Jamf, Microsoft Intune).

**Acceptance evidence:** Run the full journey on every matrix cell: macOS 13 and the current macOS release on Apple silicon, macOS 13 on Intel, Windows 10 22H2 x64, Windows 11 x64 and Windows 11 ARM64.
On each, install (including one silent MDM install per OS), sign in, open an online-only Office file from Finder/Explorer, save and observe its new server version from a second device.

In the browser, restore version 2 of that file as version 4 under VERSION-001; each client receives version 4 as a remote change, keeps the same file identity and downloads bytes whose SHA-256 equals version 2.
Switch mirror/stream modes, pin a folder, sign out and uninstall with unsent edits; show exact disposition of local work.

Add a 10 GB folder online-only and see every file listed in Finder/Explorer with its name and size while the client's local disk use grows by less than 100 MB; open one 1 GB file and see only that file downloaded, then choose Free up space on it and see local disk use fall back while the file stays listed.
Pinned files open/edit offline and reconcile automatically on reconnect.
Divergent local/cloud copies, case-only renames, moved parents, delete-versus-edit and mirror/stream cutover preserve both conflicting byte versions with named conflicts for human resolution.
A reconnect never uses an outdated permission grant; denied uploads preserve a private local recovery copy without republishing remotely.
**Acceptance evidence:** Edit a pinned file offline while another staff member changes it remotely, switch sync mode and reconnect; inspect both originals and resolve explicitly.
Repeat delete-versus-edit, case rename and permission revocation, proving no silent overwrite or unauthorized remote write.
Users see queued/uploading/downloading/conflicted/paused/failed/up-to-date states, byte progress, last successful contact and an actionable reason per file.
Admins see stale devices, client versions and unresolved errors; they can revoke a device, pause a folder and request a scoped cache wipe.
Wipe status distinguishes requested, acknowledged and unreachable; downloaded copies cannot be promised remotely erased.

**Network settings:** the client uses the system proxy by default and accepts a manual HTTP(S) proxy or PAC URL with basic, NTLM or Kerberos proxy authentication; users set upload and download bandwidth limits (unlimited, automatic or a fixed KB/s), and admins can set or cap them per group through MDM-managed configuration, which the user cannot exceed.
The client shows the active proxy and limits and names a proxy failure as the reason a file is waiting.

**Storage limits:** when a QUOTA-001 limit refuses an upload, the tray and each held file show the refusal naming the limit's scope, the limit and the current usage; unsent changes stay queued locally and upload automatically, without user action, once usage is under the limit.

At the SCALE-001 reference size, a device that was offline for 7 days catches up on 10,000 remote changes within the SCALE-001 sync target, and the admin console lists every device in the installation.
**Acceptance evidence:** Disconnect a device during transfer, exceed its cache/disk quota and revoke it; its tray and admin console show accurate unfinished work and last contact.
Resolve the cause and verify hashes before showing up-to-date; an unreachable wipe stays unconfirmed.
On macOS and Windows behind an authenticating proxy with direct egress blocked, the client syncs through the proxy; a wrong proxy password shows the proxy as the reason.
Set an upload limit of 1,000 KB/s and measure sustained upload at or below it; an MDM cap of 500 KB/s overrides a user setting of 2,000 KB/s.

On macOS and Windows, put the signed-in user over a QUOTA-001 limit and save a new file: the upload is refused, the tray and the held file name the limit's scope, the limit and the usage, and the file stays queued; after a space manager erases content under ERASE-001 (or an admin raises the limit), the queued upload completes without user action and its hash matches.
In the SCALE-001 reference installation, take a device offline, apply 10,000 remote changes, reconnect and record catch-up time against the SCALE-001 target with final hashes matching.
Byte-range streaming opens/seeks multi-GB video/design assets without full predownload, with explicit pinned ranges and cache use.

Adobe Creative Cloud, AutoCAD and Final Cut Pro work through the mounted filespace with tested save/rename semantics and app-aware locks; a second writer sees the lock, and stale leases require explicit recovery with unsent changes retained.
Browser open-in-native-app saves a new version to the same identity.
**Acceptance evidence:** Open and seek a large video in Final Cut Pro, save a Photoshop asset and AutoCAD drawing from two clients, record transferred ranges and verify final checksums/version IDs.
Compete for a lock, kill its holder and recover without losing either writer; open the same file from its browser page.
An owner can deploy an on-premises cache/storage connector for branch-office shared files, with encrypted credentials, configured folder scope, quotas and health reporting.
LAN and cloud clients use the same IDs, permissions and history; an offline cache does not turn stale ACLs into unlimited authority, and conflicts survive reconnection.

**Acceptance evidence:** Connect two office clients and a remote client to a scoped cache, disconnect WAN and expire offline authorization, edit permitted pinned files, then reconcile conflicts and verify all final hashes and access.
Replace the cache and recover from owner storage.
The SYNC-001 client also backs up folders that already live on the computer:
Desktop, Documents, Pictures, Downloads and any other local folder the user adds, as Google Drive for desktop and OneDrive Known Folder Move do.
Each backed-up folder becomes a folder in the user's personal area named for the device, keeps its local path, and syncs two ways or uploads only, as the user or policy chooses.

Admins enforce known-folder backup for a group, prevent it, or leave it to users, and can block named paths or file types; the client shows per-folder status (scanning, backing up, up to date, paused, error with reason) and the admin console shows each device's enrolled folders and last success.
Local deletions follow CHEST-13 trash rules and stay recoverable; versions follow CHEST-07.
On a new or wiped computer, the user signs in and restores any device's backed-up folders to their original paths or to a chosen location.

**Acceptance evidence:** On macOS 13+ and Windows 11 from the SYNC-001 matrix, enroll Desktop and Documents (one by user choice, one by an enforced admin policy), create, edit and delete local files and see new versions and trashed items on the server with the device-named folder.
Try to un-enroll the enforced folder as the user and be refused; block `*.tmp` and prove it is not uploaded.
Wipe the laptop, sign in on a second computer, restore both folders to their original paths and reconcile tree and SHA-256 hashes, and restore a deleted file from trash.
The admin console shows enrolled folders and last success for both devices.
When staff open Word, Excel or PowerPoint files (DOCX/XLSX/PPTX and legacy DOC/XLS/PPT) from the SYNC-001 mount, Chest warns them before two people's edits collide.

This covers **Microsoft 365 Apps and Office 2016, 2019, 2021 and LTSC 2024 desktop on Windows and macOS**, on every SYNC-001 matrix cell, through a Chest Office presence add-in that installs with the client and deploys silently by MDM.

**Presence:** while a file is open, Office shows "Also open by" with the names of every other person who has the same file open, whether in desktop Office on any client or in an EDIT-001 browser session.
The list updates within 10 seconds of someone opening or closing the file, and a holder who stops sending heartbeats drops off within 2 minutes.
Names are shown only to people who can see the file.
**Newer-version alert:** when another holder's save becomes a new server version, everyone else who has the file open is told within 30 seconds, naming who saved, before they save.
They can reload the new version (with their unsaved changes kept as a named copy) or keep editing.
**Choices on open:** a user can open the file read-only, move to co-authoring in the browser through EDIT-001, or take an **edit lock**.
While the lock is held, other holders' saves are refused in Office with the lock holder's name, and no conflict copy is created.
The lock releases on close, or by lease expiry with the SYNC-004 stale-lock recovery that keeps unsent changes.
**Admin policy**, per organization or group: off, presence only, presence with an offered lock, or lock on first open.
If someone saves without a lock after a newer version arrived, SYNC-002 still keeps both versions as a named conflict, never a silent overwrite.
Presence and lock state also show on the file's browser page and in the mobile app.
**Acceptance evidence:** Two staff open the same XLSX from the mount, one on macOS (Microsoft 365 Apps) and one on Windows (Office 2016), and each run is repeated with the operating systems swapped.
The second sees the first named under "Also open by" within 10 seconds.
The first saves; the second is told a newer version exists, naming the first, before saving, and reloading keeps the second's unsaved changes as a named copy.
On the lock path, the first takes the lock and the second's save is refused naming the holder, with no conflict copy created.
Kill the holder's client: the lock lapses through SYNC-004 recovery with the holder's unsent changes retained.
Open the file in an EDIT-001 browser session and see that person in desktop presence.
Under the "lock on first open" policy, the second opener is offered read-only or browser co-authoring only.
Native iOS/Android apps browse/search team folders, preview/share, scan with camera, upload photos automatically from selected albums and receive the user-approved background upload queue.
They integrate system Files/document pickers, open files in other apps and save new versions.

Every folder the user may add to has the **New** menu that creates a blank or templated document, spreadsheet or presentation (EDIT-004), and Office files open for co-authoring in the app in Collabora Online's touch editing interface (or Microsoft 365 where that is the user's EDIT-001 provider), and Google files under EDIT-002, through the same session, grants and versioning as the browser.
When a QUOTA-001 limit refuses an upload, the upload queue shows the refusal on each held item, naming the limit's scope, the limit and the current usage.
Users pin selected files for offline edits; device locks, local encryption, revocation and explicit offline-grant expiry protect cached business data.
Supported matrix:

**iOS and iPadOS 17 or later** (arm64, iPhone and iPad) with a File Provider extension, and **Android 10 (API level 29) or later** on arm64-v8a with a Storage Access Framework DocumentsProvider; each new major OS release joins the matrix within 90 days of general availability.
Apps ship through the Apple App Store and Google Play, with managed configuration through Microsoft Intune and Jamf.
On Chromebooks with Google Play (current ChromeOS stable), the Android app installs and its DocumentsProvider appears in the ChromeOS Files app, so ChromeOS apps open and save Chest files;
Chromebook users otherwise use the browser.
Chest ships no separate ChromeOS client.

**Acceptance evidence:** Run the journey on an iPhone on iOS 17, an iPhone on the current iOS release, an iPad on the current iPadOS, an Android 10 device and an Android device on the current release.

On each, capture a multi-page scan, upload photos, share with a permitted recipient, open/save through a system picker, create a blank spreadsheet from the New menu and co-edit it in Collabora Online with a browser user (EDIT-001), with no participant holding a Microsoft or Google license, until both edits appear as attributed versions, and edit a pinned file offline while another device changes it.
Put the user over a QUOTA-001 limit and upload a photo: the upload queue shows it refused, naming the limit's scope, the limit and the usage.
Reconnect, resolve the conflict and revoke the device; show the limit of an unreachable cache wipe.
On a Play-enabled Chromebook on current ChromeOS stable, install the Android app, open a Chest file from the ChromeOS Files app in a ChromeOS app, save it and see the new attributed version.

Create file and folder links for named invited guests, **everyone in the organization with the link**, authenticated domains or a public audience, each only where the POLICY-001 sharing policy in force for that space and sharer allows it.

An organization link admits any signed-in staff member of the installation at viewer, commenter or editor (editor = file editor under ROLE-001) without adding them by name, and refuses guests and signed-out browsers.
It obeys the ROLE-001 no-download setting.
Opening it records the item in the colleague's recent items but creates no grant, so changing or removing the link removes their access on the next request.
Each organization link is either **discoverable** or not, within POLICY-001.
A discoverable link lets any staff member find the item in search.
A non-discoverable one lets a colleague find it in search, recent items and Shared with me only after they have opened the link.
Every new link starts at the default audience and role POLICY-001 sets for the sharer's group; changing that default affects only links created afterwards.

Sharers choose password, expiry, allowed versions (current, approved-only or pinned), the link's role (viewer with or without download, commenter, or for named guests the SHARE-005 editor and contributor roles) and download-count limits; revocation and policy changes apply to every request, including old preview URLs.
Folder changes cannot expose restricted descendants.
Only password hashes are stored; link capabilities never appear in logs, public exports or chat previews.

Each item's link list and the sharer's Links view show every link's audience, role, expiry date and downloads used against its limit (for example "Expires Nov 30 · 3 of 10 downloads"), and offer **Revoke** as one action that ends the link on the next request.

**Acceptance evidence:** Share a restricted folder and pinned approved file with an external recipient; try wrong password, wrong domain, guessed child URLs, expired/revoked links and parallel downloads at the count limit.
Confirm approved-only never reveals pending replacements and a revoked link fails on the next request.
A staff member sets a team-space file to organization-with-link at commenter, not discoverable.
A colleague with no grant opens it and comments, while a guest and a signed-out browser are refused.
Before opening the link, that colleague's search does not show the file; after opening, it does.
Switch the link to discoverable and see a third colleague find it by search.
With the no-download setting on, the colleague's download is refused while the preview works.
Remove the link and see the colleague refused on the next request.
Change the admin default link audience from restricted to organization and see the next new link start at organization while existing links keep their audience.
Give a link a 10-download limit and a 30 November expiry and download through it three times: the sharer's link list shows "Expires Nov 30 · 3 of 10 downloads".
One Revoke click in that list, with no further step, makes the next request through the link fail.
Run the browser steps at 1440 and 390.
Staff issue upload-only request links for a destination, checklist, allowed types/sizes, deadline and submitter verification policy.

A recipient without a Chest seat can send resumable large files, receive a receipt and replace their own submission when allowed, without listing/downloading others or choosing a destination outside the grant.
Quarantine and late/duplicate handling are visible; closing the request stops new acceptance.
**Acceptance evidence:** Send a vendor request, submit from a signed-out phone, interrupt/resume a large upload and receive its receipt.
Try another submitter’s files, path traversal, disallowed content and an expired/closed request; verify none grants library access.
Create a version-pinned large-file transfer package with resumable downloads, expiry, count limits and optional receipt confirmation.
Link owners see attributed authenticated views, anonymous views, completed byte transfers and explicit recipient confirmations as distinct events.
Notifications never label provider acknowledgment or a preview-bot request as proof a human received the file.
**Acceptance evidence:** Send a multi-GB package to an invited recipient and a public recipient; interrupt/resume download, exercise the limit and inspect view/download/confirmation events.
A mail scanner GET and successful email API response must not set human receipt;
expiry stops new range requests.

Any staff member shares a file or folder from their personal area, and any editor or content manager shares a space item (ROLE-001), with named colleagues or groups at viewer, commenter or editor, with an optional message, subject to POLICY-001.

Recipients get an in-app notice and an email, and Slack/Teams where connected (FOLLOW-001), and find the item under **Shared with me**, filterable by sharer and date, with add-to-my-area shortcuts that grant nothing further.
A signed-in person who opens a link they cannot use sees **Request access** with an optional message and requested role, never the item's name or contents beyond what the link already reveals.

The request goes to the item's sharers with share rights (owner, file editors, then space managers); each can approve at the requested or a lower role, or decline, from the email, the in-app notice or the share dialog, and the requester is told the outcome.

A request whose owner has left or been deactivated routes to the new content owner set at offboarding (SPACE-001), then to the space managers, then to admins with content-recovery scope (ADMIN-003); it never stalls silently.
Requests expire after 30 days with the requester notified, and each request, decision and grant is audited.
**Grant expiry:** any person or group grant made here, on a personal-area or space item, can carry an optional expiry date, set when sharing or later, with admins able to set a maximum.
The sharer and the grantee get an in-app and email notice one day before expiry.
Either notice offers the sharer a one-step extend, within the maximum.
From the first request after expiry, every door refuses the grant: list, Shared with me, search, preview, download, sync hydration, editor sessions, comment and API.
The expiry is audited, and the grantee keeps any other grant they hold.
**Acceptance evidence:** Share a personal-area file with a colleague at commenter; they receive the notice and email, find it under Shared with me and can comment but not edit.
An unauthorized colleague opens the link, sees Request access without the title, requests editor; the owner approves at viewer from the email link and the requester is told and can now view.
A second request is declined from the share dialog and the requester is told.
Deactivate the owner of a third file and request access; the request reaches the new content owner, and with none, a space manager.
Grant a colleague commenter on a space file with a 2-day expiry and advance a controlled clock.
The one-day notice reaches the sharer and the grantee, and an extend from the notice moves the date once; let the new date pass.
List, preview, download, sync hydration on the colleague's client, and comment are each refused on the next request, and the audit records the expiry.
Repeat at 1440 and 390 and inspect the audit entries.

Named guests outside the organization, with or without a Google or Microsoft account, receive viewer, commenter, editor or contributor roles on a file or folder (ROLE-001) where POLICY-001 allows external sharing to their domain.

Guests sign in with a one-time PIN sent to the invited email address or with a verified Google or Microsoft identity matching it, and re-verify after an admin-set interval (default 7 days, range 1–30); a forwarded invitation alone admits no one else.
Sharers set a guest expiry date per grant and admins set a maximum; on expiry every door refuses the guest on the next request.
Guests cannot re-share or invite others; onward sharing is off and has no setting in this delivery.

Guests co-edit Office files in the shipped Collabora Online editor (EDIT-001), which needs no Microsoft or Google account or license, and upload into folders they hold contributor or editor on, and every guest edit, upload, comment and version carries the guest's verified email in version history, comments and audit.

Guest editors on a file and guest contributors on a folder can browse and download retained versions within their download grant, restore any retained version as current, upload replacements and name or rename versions under VERSION-001.

A restore creates a new version attributed to the guest's verified email, retains all later versions and keeps the stable ID, links, grants and comment threads; on a governed file it is a new submission and never moves the approved pointer without approval.
Guest viewers and commenters cannot restore, replace or name versions.
Guests hold no seat, see only what they are granted and cannot browse, search or list anything else.
**Acceptance evidence:** Invite a guest at another domain with no Google or Microsoft account as editor on a DOCX and contributor on a folder, with a 3-day expiry and re-sharing off.

The guest signs in by PIN, co-edits the DOCX with a staff member in Collabora Online under EDIT-001, on an installation with no Microsoft or Google provider configured, and uploads two files into the folder; version history and audit attribute each change to the guest's email.

For both the guest editor and the guest contributor, retain three versions, download version 2 and compare its SHA-256, name it and restore it as version 4; its bytes equal version 2, all earlier versions remain downloadable and the stable ID and existing link now serve version 4.
Version history and audit name the guest's verified email and source version once.
On a governed file, the guest's restore is a new submission and the approved pointer is unchanged.
Guest viewers and commenters are refused restore, replacement and version naming with no new version or renamed history.
Revoke the editor and refuse their next restore, replacement and rename.
The guest's attempts to share onward, open a sibling folder, search the library and use the PIN from a second email address are refused.
Advance a controlled clock past re-verification and see a new PIN required, then past expiry and see every door, including an open editor session's next save and a range request, refused.

Admins with sharing-policy scope (ADMIN-003) set an organization sharing policy, with overrides per space and per group, that states: whether sharing outside the organization is allowed at all; a trusted-domain allowlist that, when on, limits external grants and links to listed domains; whether public (anyone-with-the-link) links are allowed; whether shared-space content may be shared with people who are not members of that space; whether editors (not only managers) may share; and whether users see a warning naming the external recipients before sharing outside the organization.

It also states the **default audience and role for new links** (restricted to people added by name, organization-with-link, or public where public links are allowed) per organization and per organizational group, which the share dialog, API and every connector start from; and whether organization links may be **discoverable** in colleagues' search (SHARE-001).
A changed default applies only to links created afterwards.
Who may create team spaces, and the settings new spaces start with, are SPACE-002.
fragments.note: duplicate: a cross-reference to SPACE-002, which states who creates spaces and the settings new spaces start with

fragments.text: The most restrictive applicable rule wins where space and group overrides conflict, and the share dialog explains which rule refused or warned.

Policy is enforced at every share door: share dialog, API, SHARE-001–005, Slack/Teams (CONNECT-001/002), email add-ins (CONNECT-008), automation apps (CONNECT-009), Google Meet filing, the Calendar add-on and the Chat app (CONNECT-010) and agents.

Tightening the policy applies to existing grants and links on their next request: out-of-policy links stop working with a policy-refusal page, out-of-policy guests are suspended rather than deleted, and the admin sees the list of suspended grants to remove or re-allow.
Every policy change is audited with before and after values.
**Acceptance evidence:** Set an allowlist of one partner domain with public links off.
As staff, a share to a non-allowlisted domain and a public link are refused in the UI and API with the policy named; a share to the allowlisted domain succeeds after the external-recipient warning.
Create a public link and a non-allowlisted guest grant under a looser policy, tighten the policy and prove both are refused on the next request and listed as suspended.
Set a space override that blocks sharing outside its members while the organization allows it, and see a member's share to another colleague refused.
Confirm the same refusals through the CONNECT-007 API and a CONNECT-009 action.
Set the organization default link audience to restricted and a group default to organization-with-link at viewer.
A group member's new link starts at organization viewer and a non-member's at restricted; links created before the change keep their audience.
Turn organization-link discovery off and see a request for a discoverable organization link refused with the policy named.
Permission-checked browser/mobile previews, with pages, thumbnails and seek controls where applicable, cover this named matrix:
**documents** PDF, DOC/DOCX, XLS/XLSX, PPT/PPTX, ODT/ODS/ODP, RTF, Apple Pages/Numbers/Keynote, Google Docs/Sheets/Slides/Drawings, EML/MSG;
**text** TXT, CSV, TSV, MD, JSON, XML and common source code;
**images** JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, HEIC/HEIF, TIFF, BMP, SVG (rendered as a sanitized raster) and camera RAW (DNG, CR2/CR3, NEF, ARW);
**video** MP4 and MOV in H.264, HEVC/H.265 and Apple ProRes 422/4444, plus WebM (VP9/AV1) and AVI, played through a transcoded H.264 streaming proxy with seek;
**audio** MP3, WAV, AAC/M4A, FLAC, AIFF and OGG;
**design and CAD** PSD/PSB, AI, EPS, INDD (embedded preview), Sketch, DWG and DXF (AutoCAD 2000 through 2018 formats), STL and OBJ;
**archives** ZIP listing without extraction.
Formats outside the matrix show a named unsupported state.

Separate bounded processing services retain original bytes, exact source-version identity, renderer provenance and visible pending/failed/unsupported states; rendering does not execute file macros or widen permissions.

**Acceptance evidence:** Open one fixture per matrix format from the file page in the browser at 1440 and 390 and in both mobile apps, checking page count, first-page thumbnail and, for video/audio, seek to a mid-file timestamp; a format outside the matrix shows the unsupported state with download.
Revoke access while a preview is open and request fresh pages/ranges; deny them.
Test corrupt/malicious files and processor outage, expose the exact failure and keep the original downloadable to an authorized user.
Extract searchable text from every admitted file in this named matrix, retaining source version, parser/language, confidence and extraction state:
**OCR** of image-only PDF pages and JPEG, PNG, TIFF, HEIC and WebP images in English and Spanish (other languages indexed with their detected language recorded);

**text extraction** from PDF text layers, DOC/DOCX, XLS/XLSX, PPT/PPTX, ODT/ODS/ODP, RTF, Apple Pages/Numbers/Keynote, Google Docs/Sheets/Slides via export, EML/MSG bodies and attachments, TXT, CSV, MD, HTML, JSON and XML;
**transcripts** of English and Spanish speech in MP4, MOV, MP3, WAV and M4A.
The full extracted text of each version is indexed; any truncation is shown as partially indexed with the offset reached.
Search spans names, content, typed metadata, owners, dates, folders and versions with snippets, and meets the SCALE-001 search target at the reference size.
Unsupported or encrypted files visibly remain unindexed.
Current permissions govern hits, snippets, counts, suggestions and AI retrieval; revocation supersedes stale indexes.
**Filters** appear as chips under the search box.
Each can be used alone, with others, or with text:
**Type:** folders; documents (DOC/DOCX, ODT, RTF, Pages, Google Docs, TXT, MD); spreadsheets (XLS/XLSX, ODS, CSV, TSV, Numbers, Google Sheets); presentations (PPT/PPTX, ODP, Keynote, Google Slides);
PDFs; images; videos; audio; archives; and other.
Type is matched on the file type detected from content, not the extension alone, so a PDF renamed `.txt` counts as a PDF.
Several types can be chosen at once.
**People:** owned by me, owned by a named person, created by a named person, or shared with me by a named person.
**Modified:** today, last 7 days, last 30 days, this year, last year, or a custom from–to range in the user's US time zone.
**Location:** anywhere, a chosen space or folder including its subfolders, my personal area, Shared with me, Starred, or Trash for those allowed to see it.
**Version:** current versions only (the default) or any retained version.
A match found only in an earlier version is labeled with that version.
Filters combine with AND across filters and OR within one filter's choices.
A search with filters and no text lists the matching files, newest first.

Filters work in the browser at 1440 and 390, in the iOS and Android apps, and through the CONNECT-007 search API as named parameters (`type`, `owner`, `creator`, `sharedBy`, `modifiedFrom`, `modifiedTo`, `location`, `versions`).
Filter counts and folder suggestions follow current access exactly as hits do: a file the user cannot open is never counted, suggested or used to suggest a person.

**Acceptance evidence:** Upload one fixture per matrix format, each holding a distinctive phrase (including a scanned English invoice, a scanned Spanish receipt, an Office spreadsheet, a Google document, an MSG with a DOCX attachment, a spoken-phrase MP4 and an encrypted PDF), find every phrase and filter by folder/version.
Then seed files that all contain one shared phrase:
PDFs, spreadsheets and images; files owned by two different people; files modified 3 days and 40 days ago; one PDF renamed `.txt`; and one matching PDF in a folder a test user cannot open.
Search the phrase with Type = PDF, People = owned by the second owner and Modified = last 30 days.
Only the matching files come back, including the renamed PDF.
Combine each of Type, People, Modified and Version with Location = Shared with me, and again with Location = one space; check each result set against the seed.
Use a custom date range, and a filter-only search with no text.
The test user never sees the PDF they cannot open, or a count or suggestion that includes it.
Repeat in the browser at 1440 and 390, in the iOS and Android apps and through the search API.
Show OCR provenance and the encrypted-file gap; revoke a group before index refresh and prove zero leaked snippets/counts/autocomplete through search API and UI.
Repeat a fixed query set in the SCALE-001 reference installation and record latency against the SCALE-001 search target.

When a scanned or photographed document arrives (an image-only PDF page, or a JPEG, PNG, TIFF, HEIC or WebP image, read by SEARCH-001 OCR), Chest reads the values of the CHEST-02 typed fields defined for its type: for an NDA, the parties, effective date, term and governing state; for a W-9, the legal name, business type and the last four digits of the TIN, shown masked; for an invoice, the vendor, number, date and USD total.

The file page shows the scan with a box drawn around the words each value came from, with its page, the value and a confidence, in the browser at desktop and phone widths and in the iOS and Android apps.
Read values are proposals until a person who can edit the file confirms, corrects or rejects each one.
Confirmed values become ordinary typed fields, with provenance naming the version, page, region and reader.
Chest never overwrites a value a person entered: a differing reading is shown beside it.
It never fills a required field without confirmation, and it reads again only when a new version arrives, keeping earlier confirmations on their own version.
Low-confidence and unreadable fields are shown as such, never guessed.
Read values are visible only to people who can open the file and follow CHEST-06 in lists, counts and search.
The reading service, its spend and its data retention are owner-selected under AGENT-007, and text inside a document is data, never an instruction.
**Acceptance evidence:** Upload a two-page scanned NDA (image-only PDF) into a folder whose type defines Party, Effective date, Term and Governing state, and a phone photo of a W-9.
On each file page at 1440 and 390 and in the iOS and Android apps, every proposed value shows its page, a box around its source words and a confidence.

An editor confirms two NDA values, corrects one and rejects one; the typed fields, a SEARCH-001 search and the audit then show the confirmed values with version, page and region provenance, and the rejected one is not stored.
A value a person had already typed is left unchanged, with the differing reading shown beside it.
A deliberately blurred field is shown as unreadable and left empty.
A viewer sees the confirmed values but has no confirm control, and their API confirm is refused with 403.
An outsider's search for a read value returns nothing.
Upload a new version with a changed effective date: only that field is proposed again, and the earlier confirmations stay on the earlier version.

Chest ships **Collabora Online** as its included independent office editor, so staff and guests co-author DOCX, XLSX and PPTX (and ODT, ODS and ODP) when no one holds a Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace license.
Chest's installer deploys Collabora Online as a separately run service and Chest is its WOPI host.
Once the owner confirms it at setup, it is the default provider for opening and creating office files.
**Microsoft 365** (Office for the web and desktop Office) is an optional second provider through the Microsoft Cloud Storage Partner Program WOPI integration.
An admin with service-settings scope (ADMIN-003) enables it for the organization or named groups.
Google types are EDIT-002.
A file is open for editing in one provider at a time, and Chest never rebuilds an office engine.
**Sessions:** current file grants, including SHARE-005 guest editor and contributor grants, scope every editing session.
Saves keep format fidelity and the file's stable identity, and each save is an immutable version attributed to its author (VERSION-001, arrival "editor save").
Revoking a grant refuses that person's next save and ends their session.
Everyone in a session sees the names of the others editing, on the document and on the file page.
Co-authors edit the one file: a session never creates a copy, a conflict file or a second stable ID.
**Browser and mobile:** co-authoring works in the browser at desktop and phone widths and in the iOS and Android apps (MOBILE-001).
The apps open Collabora Online's touch editing interface inside the app, on the same WOPI session, grants and attributed saves as the browser.
Where Microsoft 365 is the user's provider, they open the Microsoft 365 mobile apps or Office for the web instead.

**Microsoft licenses:** Chest uses the CSPP business-user flow with WOPI license checking on, so Office for the web verifies that each editor holds a Microsoft 365 license that includes Office for the web.
A user without one gets the read-only Office for the web view, with "Editing needs a Microsoft 365 license that includes Office for the web" shown as the reason.
They never get a broken editor or an unlicensed editing session.
Where Collabora Online is also enabled, that view offers **Edit in Collabora Online** whenever no Microsoft session holds the file.
**Capacity and cost:** before either provider is enabled, at setup or later, the ADMIN-002 console shows:
its edition:
Collabora Online Development Edition (CODE) or a Collabora Online subscription, or for Microsoft the license each editor must hold;
its limits on concurrent open documents and connections;
its USD cost: $0 for CODE, or the per-user annual price the owner enters from their Collabora or Microsoft quote, labeled as an owner-entered estimate.

When CODE is chosen, the console states before confirmation that Collabora positions CODE for development and home use, not supported business production, shows the document and connection limits that CODE reports, and lists what a Collabora Online subscription adds as named in the owner's quote (vendor support and maintained releases).
The owner must acknowledge this to enable CODE, and the console keeps the notice on show while CODE is in use.
Chest enforces the configured limits itself.
An editing session past a limit is refused with `editor_capacity_reached`, naming the limit and current use, in the browser, the mobile apps and the API.
The file opens in the read-only preview instead, and sessions already open continue.
Usage against each limit is in ADMIN-002 reports.
**Loss of provider:** an editor outage or a lapsed subscription or license is shown by name on the file and in the console.
Originals stay downloadable and portable, and nothing in an unsaved session is presented as saved.

**Download as another format:** anyone allowed to download an office file downloads its current or any listed version as PDF, or as DOCX or ODT, XLSX or ODS, PPTX or ODP, from the file page at both widths, the iOS and Android apps and the CONNECT-007 API.
Chest converts through the shipped Collabora Online service, names the source version in the file name and the audit entry, and never stores the converted copy as a new version.
The ROLE-001 no-download setting refuses every format.

**Link to a Chest file:** in an editing session in the browser at both widths and in the iOS and Android apps, Chest adds an **Insert Chest link** command to Collabora Online's toolbar and Insert menu, with a keyboard shortcut, through Collabora's PostMessage integration.
It searches Chest (SEARCH-001) for files and folders the author can currently open and inserts a link to the item's stable Chest URL, with the item's name as the link text.
A link opens under the reader's current access, and a reader without access sees the SHARE-004 Request access page.

Inserting a link grants nothing: when people who can open the document cannot open the linked item, the author is told who and offered a one-step grant where ROLE-001 and POLICY-001 let the author share, or the refusal with the rule named.
A pasted Chest URL behaves the same.

**Review loop in the shipped editor:** in Collabora Online, for DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, ODT, ODS and ODP, in the browser at both widths and in the iOS and Android apps, Chest carries the review workflow Google Docs users run.
Chest is the integrator for all of it: it supplies the people list, records each comment, mention, assignment and tracked change against Chest identities and sends every notification.
It never relies on a file format's own mention markup, so the behavior is the same in every listed format.
A format or Collabora release in which any part below does not work fails this clause's acceptance; making it work
, in Chest's integration or upstream
fragments.note: the "in Chest's integration or upstream" duty, an open-ended obligation to patch a third-party engine rather than a buyer outcome (RL-17)

fragments.text: , is delivery work under this clause.
**Attribution:** every comment, reply, resolve and tracked change carries the author's Chest name, or a SHARE-005 guest's verified email, set by Chest for the session.
A save that adds or alters a comment or tracked change under any other author is refused with `author_mismatch`, creates no version and is audited.
**@mentions:** typing `@` in a comment suggests only the people and groups the author may share the file with under POLICY-001, listing first those who can already open it.
Posting the comment sends the FOLLOW-001 mention notification, with the comment text and a link to it, to each mentioned person and each member of a mentioned group who can open the file.
A mentioned person without access is sent nothing.

The author is instead offered a one-step grant at commenter or viewer where ROLE-001 and POLICY-001 let the author share; otherwise Chest explains the refusal, naming the rule, and offers to send a SHARE-004 access request for that person to the file's managers.
An address typed on a domain POLICY-001 does not allow is refused with the policy named.
A mention never grants access silently (EDIT-003).

**Assigned comments:** inside the editor's comment box, as with Google Docs' "Assign to", the author assigns a comment by mentioning one person and choosing **Assign**; the file page and the apps offer the same control on the thread.
A comment can be assigned to one person who can open the file, or to someone without access after the same grant step.

The assignee is notified, and the comment is an open task in their EDIT-003 and FOLLOW-001 task lists, with FOLLOW-001 reminders, until it is resolved in the document, on the file page, in the apps or from the notification email.
Reassigning moves the task and notifies both people.
**One thread at every door:** each in-document comment is an EDIT-003 thread on the file page and in the mobile apps, anchored to the version and to the commented text, cell or slide.
A comment, reply, resolve or reopen made in an editing session reaches its thread and its notifications within 60 seconds, without anyone closing the document.

A reply or resolve made on the file page, in the apps or from the FOLLOW-001 email appears in the document: in every open session within 60 seconds, and in the file as a new version attributed to that person with arrival "comment reply" or "comment resolved".
Where a format cannot store a comment's resolved state, Chest keeps it on the thread and shows it in the editor.
**Commenters suggest, contributors decide:** a ROLE-001 commenter, a file commenter or a SHARE-005 guest commenter opens Collabora Online in a comment-and-suggest session, not a read-only view.
In documents (DOCX and ODT), change tracking is on and locked: their typing is recorded as tracked changes attributed to them, never as direct edits, and they cannot accept, reject or stop tracking.
In spreadsheets and presentations, where Google Sheets and Slides give commenters no suggesting mode either, the session is comment-only.

Chest checks every save from such a session against the version it opened and refuses with `suggest_only`, creating no version, any save that changes anything other than comments and that person's own tracked changes.
Pending suggestions are listed on the file page and in the apps with author and age, and the file's owner, or the space's managers, get the FOLLOW-001 notification of new suggestions.
Contributors and above, file editors and guest editors accept or reject each suggestion in the editor.
Each decision is saved as its own version, attributed to the decider and naming the suggestion's author and the decision (VERSION-001).
A viewer's session is read-only, with no comment or suggest control, and any save from it is refused.
New files start in the user's editor from the New menu (EDIT-004).

**Acceptance evidence:** On an installation with no Microsoft or Google provider configured, where no participant holds a Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace license, using the shipped Collabora Online:
At setup, the console shows Collabora Online's edition, its document and connection limits and its USD cost before the owner confirms enabling it.
Choosing CODE shows the not-for-production notice and what a subscription adds, and enabling it is refused until the owner acknowledges the notice.
Two staff and one PIN-verified SHARE-005 guest co-edit a DOCX, an XLSX and a PPTX in the browser at 1440 and 390.
Concurrent changes reach every participant, and each save is a version attributed to its author, the guest by verified email.
While they co-edit, each participant sees the other two named as present in the editor and on the file page.
Afterwards the folder holds one file with one stable ID and no copy or conflict file, and its version history attributes each person's saves.
Revoke the guest mid-session and see their next save refused.
Repeat one co-edit with one participant in the iOS app and one in the Android app on the MOBILE-001 current-release devices, each save attributed to that participant.
Revoke the Android participant mid-session and see their next save refused.
Round-trip tables, formulas and comments in all three formats, then open the saved versions in desktop Word, Excel and PowerPoint and in LibreOffice with them intact.
Edit a review-gated file and see its approved version unchanged.
Stop the Collabora Online service and see the outage named, with the original still downloadable.
A contributor creates a blank spreadsheet from the EDIT-004 New menu, and it opens in Collabora Online.
A uses Insert Chest link in the DOCX, searches for a contract in a restricted folder A can open and inserts it; a search for a file A cannot open returns nothing.
A is told that staff member B, who can open the DOCX but not that folder, cannot open the link, and is offered a viewer grant;
A declines, and B following the link sees Request access.
Repeat at 390 and in the iOS and Android apps.
A viewer downloads the DOCX as PDF and as ODT from the file page, the iOS app and the API, each named for its source version, with no new version created.
With the ROLE-001 no-download setting on, each format is refused.
Review loop, on the same installation:
Staff A opens a DOCX and comments "@B please check clause 4".
B gets the in-app and email notifications with the comment text, and the comment shows A and B by Chest name in the editor and on the file page.
A mentions C, who has no access to the file.
A is offered a commenter grant, and C is sent nothing until A accepts it;
C is then notified and opens the file.
A contributor in a space with editor sharing switched off mentions D, who has no access: the refusal names the rule, and the offered access request reaches the file's managers.
A mention of an address on a domain outside the POLICY-001 allowlist is refused with the policy named, and autocomplete never offered it.
Inside the Collabora Online comment box, A mentions B in a new comment and chooses Assign, and the comment appears in B's task list.
B replies to the notification email: within 60 seconds the reply appears inside A's open session, attributed to B, and the file gains a "comment reply" version.
B resolves the comment on the file page and it shows resolved inside the document.
A replies inside the document and the thread on the file page shows it within 60 seconds.
A PIN-verified SHARE-005 guest commenter opens the DOCX and types a change.
It is recorded as a tracked change attributed to their verified email, and the file's owner is notified of the suggestion.
Saves from that session carrying a direct edit, and one adding a comment under B's name, are refused with `suggest_only` and `author_mismatch` and create no version.
A contributor accepts one of the guest's suggestions and rejects another, and each decision is its own version attributed to the contributor, naming the guest and the decision.
A viewer's session is read-only, and a save from it is refused.
Repeat the @mention step with an XLSX comment, a PPTX comment and an ODT, and the guest suggestion step with the ODT.
In the XLSX and the PPTX, the commenter's comment posts and their cell or slide edit is refused with `suggest_only`.
Run every review-loop step in the browser at 1440 and 390 and in the iOS and Android apps on the MOBILE-001 current-release devices.
Set the connection limit to 3 and open a fourth editing session: it is refused with `editor_capacity_reached`, naming the limit and current use, in the browser, a mobile app and the API.
The file opens read-only, and the three open sessions continue.
Then enable Microsoft 365 for one group in a CSPP test tenant:
Two licensed users co-edit a DOCX, an XLSX and a PPTX through Office for the web and desktop Office, with attributed saves.
Revoke one mid-session and see their next save refused.
A group member without a qualifying license opens the same DOCX and gets the read-only view with the license named as the reason.
No editing session is created, and no save from them is accepted.
With no Microsoft session open on the file, they choose Edit in Collabora Online, and their saves are attributed to them.

Google Workspace Docs, Sheets and Slides integration opens/co-edits native content with explicit source custody and granted scopes, saves revision provenance and exports portable Office/PDF derivatives.
Migration can convert to Chest-hosted editable formats with a fidelity report; a shortcut alone never counts as a migrated original.
Provider-required features remain disclosed until the owner accepts conversion or continued provider use.

A conversion, at migration or later, carries the file's open review work under MIGRATE-002's open-review-work rules: comments become EDIT-003 threads with their authors, open or resolved states and assignees, and pending suggestions become tracked changes.
A file kept native keeps its comments and suggestions in Google, and Chest shows them as provider-held without duplicating them.
**Acceptance evidence:** Create and co-edit each Google type from Chest with two accounts, then export/convert a file containing comments, formulas and embedded content.
