The converted file's comments are EDIT-003 threads attributed to the mapped people under MIGRATE-002's author rule, open or resolved as in the source, its assigned comments are open tasks for their assignees, and its pending suggestions are tracked changes that a contributor accepts or rejects as EDIT-001 decision versions; the fidelity report counts each against the source.
Reconcile unsupported features, revoke source access and prove that accepted Chest-held originals/derivatives remain accessible with accurate source and revision labels.
Files support threaded comments, mentions, resolved tasks and PDF page/region annotations, bound to the exact version.
Users can compare versions, navigate unresolved comments and carry a thread forward only with an explicit link to its original.

Comments made inside office files in the shipped EDIT-001 editor are EDIT-003 threads too: one thread per in-document comment, kept in step both ways under EDIT-001's review loop, with the same mentions, assignments and resolution, on the file page and in the mobile apps.
An assigned comment is a task in the assignee's list until it is resolved.
Mentioning or assigning a person never grants them access.

Threads migrated from an incumbent (MIGRATE-001/002) keep their original timestamps, source IDs and open or resolved state, show an author who could not be matched as "Former collaborator (name as in source)" and keep the quoted text of a comment whose anchor was not found; they then behave as any other thread.
**Acceptance evidence:** Annotate page 2 of a PDF, mention an authorized colleague and an outsider, resolve a thread and upload a changed-page replacement.
The old annotation remains anchored to its original, notifications contain no forbidden text and the outsider gains no access.

Then, in Collabora Online, comment inside a DOCX with a mention and an assignment: the thread appears on the file page and in the iOS and Android apps, anchored to the version and the commented text, and the task appears in the assignee's list.
Resolve it on the file page and see it resolved inside the document and gone from the task list (EDIT-001).

Open a file migrated under MIGRATE-002: its migrated threads show their original timestamps and states, a former collaborator's comment is attributed to no current person and cannot be re-attributed by a save, an "anchor not found" thread shows its quoted text, and replying to and resolving a migrated thread work as on any other.
Every folder a user may add to shows a **New** menu, beside New folder and Upload, in the browser at desktop and phone widths and in the iOS and Android apps (MOBILE-001).

It creates a blank **document, spreadsheet or presentation** in that folder, or one from a template, and the new file opens at once in the user's EDIT-001 editor: the shipped Collabora Online by default, or Microsoft 365 for the web where it is enabled for the user's group and the user holds a qualifying license (an unlicensed user's new file opens in Collabora Online when it is enabled, and otherwise read-only with the license reason).
It may also open as a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file under EDIT-002 when the organization uses that provider for new files.
The same create is in the CONNECT-007 API ("create file from blank or template"), idempotent on a caller key.
**Creation format:** admins with service-settings scope (ADMIN-003) set the format for new files for the organization, with group overrides:
**DOCX, XLSX and PPTX by default**, ODT, ODS and ODP as an option, or native Google types where EDIT-002 is enabled.
A blank file is a valid empty file of that format that opens without repair in desktop Microsoft Office and LibreOffice through the SYNC-001 mount.

**Templates:** a built-in gallery in each creation format (at least letter, memo, meeting notes, project proposal, invoice, budget, project tracker, schedule and two presentation designs), plus **organization templates**.

An admin with service-settings scope, or a space manager for their own space, publishes any DOCX, XLSX, PPTX or ODF file they can view (or a Google file under EDIT-002) as a template to the whole organization, to named groups or to one space, with a name, category and thumbnail.
Only users in that audience see the template, in the New menu, the template gallery and the API listing.
Publishing gives template users no access to the source file.
Unpublishing hides the template and leaves files made from it untouched.
**Copy, not link:** creating from a template makes an independent copy.

Its version 1 holds the template's current bytes, with provenance naming the template and its version, and nothing links back: editing the new file never changes the template, and editing the template never changes files already made from it.
**The new file** gets a default name ("Untitled document", "Untitled spreadsheet", "Untitled presentation") the user can change before or after opening.
It is version 1 under VERSION-001, attributed to the creator with arrival "created", and each editor save adds a version.
It is owned by the folder's space, or by the creator's personal area, and inherits the folder's access, including restricted subfolders and the ROLE-001 no-download setting.
It appears at once in the creator's recent items, in listings and SEARCH-001 for everyone with current access, and on SYNC-001 clients as a new file.

**Who may create:** contributors, content managers and managers on a space folder, owners and file editors of a personal-area folder, and SHARE-005 guests holding contributor or editor on the folder (attributed to their verified email).
Viewers and commenters see no New action, and their create through the API is refused with 403 and no file.
QUOTA-001 applies: a create in an over-limit area is refused with `storage_limit_exceeded`.
POLICY-001 and GOVERN-001 rules on the folder apply to a new file as to an upload.
Every create, template publish and unpublish is audited.

**Acceptance evidence:** Run these journeys on an installation with no Microsoft or Google provider configured, where new files open in the shipped Collabora Online (EDIT-001), through the browser at 1440 and 390 and in the iOS and Android apps on the MOBILE-001 current-release devices.
Then enable Microsoft 365 for the web and repeat the first journey with a licensed contributor.
A contributor creates a blank spreadsheet in a restricted team-space folder.
It opens in the EDIT-001 editor at once, and after two saved edits its version history shows versions 1–3 (created, then two editor saves) attributed to them.
A colleague with folder access finds it in search and opens it; a staff member outside the folder finds nothing in search and gets 403 on its URL.
Create a blank document and a blank presentation; download each version 1 and open it in desktop Word, Excel or PowerPoint and in LibreOffice without a repair prompt.

Switch the organization creation format to ODF and see the next new document created as ODT; set a group override to Google types under EDIT-002 and see a group member's new document open as a Google Doc.
An admin publishes a DOCX organization template to one group.
A group member creates a document from it; a user outside the group does not see the template in the New menu, the gallery or the API listing.

Editing the new document leaves the template's bytes and version unchanged, editing the template afterwards leaves the new document unchanged, and the new document's version 1 names the template and its version.
A space manager publishes a space template that only that space's members see.
Unpublish the organization template and see documents made from it unchanged.
A viewer and a commenter see no New action, and their direct API create returns 403 with no file created.
A guest contributor on a folder creates a blank document there, attributed to the guest's email.
An over-limit user's create in their personal area is refused with `storage_limit_exceeded` naming the limit in the browser, the mobile app and the API.
Repeat an API create with the same caller key and get one file.
Inspect the audit entry for each create, publish and unpublish.
A staff member requests signatures on the exact current version of a PDF or DOCX from its file page in the browser or the mobile app.
This needs no third-party signature account.
They need contributor, content-manager or manager access on a space file, or editor access on a personal-area file, with download allowed.
A DOCX is rendered to PDF for signing; the rendition records its source version and comes with a fidelity report the requester sees before sending.
The requester:
adds signers by email: staff, or external people who need no Chest or Google/Microsoft account;
sets a signing order, or lets everyone sign at once;
places signature, initials, date-signed, text and checkbox fields for each signer;
sets an expiry date and a reminder cadence, sent through FOLLOW-001 and stopped on completion, decline, void or expiry.
Signers verify by a one-time PIN sent to the invited email address, as in SHARE-005, or by staff sign-in.
Before signing, each signer sees and accepts an electronic-records consent disclosure, which also explains how to withdraw consent or get a paper copy.
They adopt a signature, and sign through an explicit action, or decline with a reason.
A signer sees only the document they are asked to sign and gains no other access.

On completion Chest files two new immutable versions linked to the source version (CHEST-07), with provenance: the **signed PDF**, sealed with a PAdES digital signature under the installation's signing key in SECURITY-001 custody so any later change is detectable, and an **audit certificate**.

The certificate lists each signer's email and verification method, the IP address and user agent for every event (sent, viewed, consented, signed, declined), the timestamps, and the SHA-256 of the document before and after signing.
Every signer receives the completed copy by email link.
A declined, voided or expired request leaves the source version unchanged and unsigned, files no partial signed version, and keeps the request record with its outcome.
Signing is distinct from Chest approval (CHEST-08) and approves nothing.
Signed records are retained, and reproduced exactly for every entitled party, until an authorized erasure under ERASE-001 or GOVERN-001.
**Evidential standard claimed:** the flow is built to satisfy the US ESIGN Act (15 U.S.C. §7001 et seq.) and UETA.

That means intent to sign through an explicit adopt-and-sign action, consumer consent to electronic records before signing, the signature associated with the exact record, and retention with accurate reproduction.
Chest warns when a document appears to fall in ESIGN's excluded categories (for example wills and court notices), and it makes no claim of legal sufficiency for a particular document.
Firms that standardize on Docusign keep CONNECT-004.
Remote online notarization and EU qualified signatures are not offered here; they go through CONNECT-004.

**Acceptance evidence:** Through the browser at 1440 and 390 and the mobile app, send a two-signer PDF in order: first an external signer with no Chest or Google/Microsoft account, then a staff member.
A reminder reaches the first signer on the set cadence.
The external signer verifies by PIN, sees the consent disclosure and is refused any other file.
Both sign.

The signed PDF and the certificate appear as new versions linked to the source version, with before and after hashes and the full event log; the PAdES signature validates, and validation fails after one byte of the signed PDF is altered.
Reminders stop.
Send a DOCX request and see the fidelity report before sending.
A declined request and an expired request each leave the source version unchanged and unsigned, with no signed version filed and the outcome recorded.
A voided request stops further signing.
Restoring one file's earlier version is VERSION-001, open to every contributor and editor of that file.
Point-in-time rewind covers many files at once: a user rewinds their own files and folders; a space manager rewinds any file, folder tree or the whole space they manage.
Each previews and restores to a chosen recorded point after accidental deletion, overwrite or ransomware, with no installation owner required.
Bulk restore after a detected incident is SECURITY-003.
The preview lists changed originals, names, hierarchy, memberships and sharing effects; restoring content cannot silently re-enable revoked shares or users.
Recovery creates an attributed new state while retaining later recoverable history and conflict copies.
Admin account rewind:
ADMIN-003.

**Acceptance evidence:** Make a folder with multiple versions, rename/delete it and overwrite sibling files, then, as the space manager (not the installation owner), preview a time-based rewind and restore selected content.
Compare every restored byte/path, retain later history and prove a formerly revoked external link and staff identity remain denied.
A space viewer is refused the rewind.
An editor's folder rewind is limited to their own files, while the same editor restores a single earlier version of a colleague's file under VERSION-001.

Owners schedule encrypted independent backups to Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2 or an S3-compatible owner account outside the live sync authority, with retention, last success, failure alerts and a recovery drill.

Archives cover all new product records, originals, comments, links as inert definitions, rules, migration mappings and sanitized execution history; secrets/devices/sessions never transfer and sending jobs never replay.
Upgrades preserve configured settings and data; a failed upgrade has a documented rollback from a private backup.

**Acceptance evidence:** Back up a populated installation, corrupt the live store and restore into a clean instance, reconcile the complete graph and hashes, reauthorize providers and prove no old device/link authority or queued message replays.
Upgrade a copy of a populated prior release, inspect identity/settings/history, and recover from an interrupted upgrade.
Okta, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) and Google Workspace identity support SAML/OIDC SSO with enforced domain policy, group mapping and SCIM or the provider’s supported directory lifecycle API.

Owners preview destructive group changes, retain a protected break-glass path and transfer content/assignments before deprovisioning; disabling a user revokes web/mobile/editor/device/agent authority and external grants that depend on that identity.

A destructive group change from the provider denies the removed members' access immediately; the complete desired group snapshot is queued for the owner to preview and confirm, and the additions and renames in it wait for that confirmation.
Declining the review never silently restores access already revoked.
**Acceptance evidence:** Against a real identity provider, provision a user/group, sign in, change membership and deactivate the user.

Per the owner's direction of 17 October 2026, Run Edit Run's own Auth product (run-auth), run locally as the live OIDC/SAML/SCIM provider, proves the protocol and lifecycle; certification in each vendor's test tenant (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace) is not claimed by that journey and remains to be done.
Confirm all public doors/devices/editor sessions lose authority, team content remains owned, and a bad mapping/IdP outage does not strand the protected owner recovery path.

A provider group change that removes one member and adds another denies the removed member at once while the added member gains nothing until the owner confirms the previewed snapshot; declining the review leaves the removed member denied.
Admins filter/export user/content activity, access and sharing changes, external guests, downloads, storage by team/version/trash, sync failures, transfer usage and extraction/AI spend.
Capacity/seat limits, retention and US-dollar storage/egress/provider charges are explicit before enabling paid work; estimates are distinguished from invoices.

The cost view is provider-only: costs from the owner's own providers (hosting, storage, mail, editor subscriptions or licenses, AI spend) are shown in USD with each provider named, and never as a Chest charge (OPEN-001).

Before an office editor is enabled (EDIT-001), the console shows its edition, its concurrent-document and connection limits and its USD cost, and reports show usage against those limits and every `editor_capacity_reached` refusal.
Reports show each user's and space's usage against its storage limit; setting limits, their scope and precedence, and over-limit behavior are QUOTA-001.
For reporting, activity dates are inclusive UTC instants;
CSV exports include every matching page under current administrative scope.
Storage is a current retained-original snapshot, deduplicated by SHA-256 across selected areas.

An original is assigned once to live current, otherwise live previous, otherwise trash (including descendants of trashed folders), otherwise quarantined/rejected request custody; per-area totals can overlap and are never summed into an organization total.

Provider rates are explicitly confirmed owner-entered USD estimates, using decimal GB (1,000,000,000 bytes), a current monthly storage run rate rounded to six decimal places, and a named quote/source; they are not invoices, live prices or authority to enable paid work.
Stream receipts reserve each output chunk durably before emission.
A lost completion is uncertain, with confirmed bytes and the reserved upper bound kept separate; no restart fabricates delivery.
Organization selection totals include ZIP framing, while scoped totals include only original member bytes at the enclosing ZIP output checkpoints under current custody.

Provider-call receipts snapshot the confirmed quote at request start; reported uncached input and output tokens use decimal millions, and request fees and network estimates remain separate provider charges.
Anthropic input excludes cache units;
OpenAI prompt totals include cache reads, which are subtracted before uncached pricing.
Cache read, five minute write and one hour write quotes use decimal millions; a nonstandard provider service tier requires an exact tier quote.
Missing or malformed units and unmatched models or tiers remain unknown.

Collabora admission counts unexpired Chest session reservations of at most 30 minutes, checks document and connection ceilings atomically and records each Chest refusal; an acknowledged close releases that reservation.
Provider-side disconnection is not inferred.
EDIT-001, EDIT-002, SIGN-001, RECOVER-002, CONNECT-001 through CONNECT-010 and AGENT-007 inherit accounting for every new paid producer before shipping.
Portability receipts preserve operation-specific confirmed quotes and separate provider inbound and outbound decimal GB estimates.
Private local receipt journals contain metadata only, survive database replacement and replay idempotently; a lost completion remains uncertain.
Licensed editor limits are administrator-recorded from the quote, with product and version from an explicit audited probe.
Provider-side capacity stays unknown; browser outcomes reconcile to Chest admissions and never claim complete provider verification.
ADMIN-002 reports the configured Collabora edition, administrator-recorded licensed limits and costs, Chest reservations and refusals, and attributed observed provider outcomes.
Independent provider-side enforcement is not inferred from those records;
EDIT-001 retains live editor packaging, capacity and operation proof.
fragments.note: restates that the editor clause keeps its own proof, now explicit in EDIT-001.1 and EDIT-001.3

fragments.text: External-guest reporting is a current snapshot of shared-link audiences and retained file-request submission evidence under the same content-custody administrative scope.
Configured recipient addresses prove no visit; completed email verification is historical evidence, never a live-session count.
Domain and anonymous audiences have no known person count, and self-reported submitter addresses remain unverified.
Existing view-history privacy choices and identity-erasure redaction apply; activity date filters do not apply to this snapshot.
**Acceptance evidence:** Create activity from staff, guest, client and agent; reconcile a permission-scoped CSV report with source events and bytes including old versions/trash.
Enable Collabora Online and see its edition, limits and USD cost before confirming; drive it to its connection limit and see the refusal counted in the report.
Reach a QUOTA-001 test limit and trigger an estimated provider cost; show the warning and preserved originals, with no invented savings or live-price claim.
The cost view lists only provider costs, each labeled with its provider, and no Chest charge.

The installation owner promotes any number of staff to **super admin** (every admin action, including other admins' roles) and assigns delegated admin roles, alone or combined, each scoped to the whole organization or to named groups:
**user management** (invite, deactivate, reactivate, change groups, transfer content at offboarding);
**help desk** (resend invitations, revoke sessions and devices, reset a user's sign-in factors under ADMIN-004);
**sharing and security policy** (POLICY-001, SECURITY-002/003 settings);
**service settings** (integrations, backup, sync and mobile policy, space creation and new-space defaults under SPACE-002, and storage limits under QUOTA-001);
**content recovery** (restore across spaces under CHEST-13/RECOVER-001); and **audit and reporting** (read-only ADMIN-002/AUDIT-001).
Admins can also define custom roles from these privileges.
An admin role confers no access to file contents, names, previews or search results unless that person also holds a content role (ROLE-001);
content recovery restores items without opening them.
The owner role transfers to another super admin with the recipient's acceptance and a fresh sign-in; afterwards the former owner keeps only the roles explicitly left to them.
At least two super admins are recommended and the console warns while only one exists; the last super admin cannot be demoted or deactivated.
Every role grant, change and use is audited.
An admin with content-recovery scope rewinds a departed user's account or any space to a chosen recorded point after accidental deletion, overwrite or ransomware, without the installation owner.
The preview lists changed originals, names, hierarchy, memberships and sharing effects; the admin restores selected content without opening it or gaining a content role.
Recovery creates attributed new states, retains later recoverable history and conflict copies, and never re-enables revoked shares or identities (RECOVER-001).
**Acceptance evidence:** As owner, promote a second super admin and grant a staff member help desk scoped to one group.

The help-desk admin revokes a group member's sessions and resets their second factor, then is refused that member's file list, previews, downloads and search hits, a reset for a user outside the group, and a policy change.

Transfer ownership to the second super admin; the former owner is refused owner-only actions (installation settings, owner transfer, super-admin changes) on the next request while the new owner succeeds.
Try to demote the last super admin and be refused.
Give a different staff member content-recovery scope and no content role.

In a departed user's account and in a team space, create multiple versions, rename, move, delete and overwrite items, then have that admin preview a recorded point and restore selected content without the owner.
Compare every restored byte and path as a content-authorized colleague, retaining later history and conflict copies.

The preview accounts for membership and sharing changes; revoked links and the departed identity remain denied, and the admin still cannot list names, preview, search or download the restored content.
Remove content-recovery scope and refuse the next preview and restore.
Inspect the audit of each step.
Installations that do not federate through ADMIN-001 enforce two-step verification natively.
Factors are TOTP authenticator apps, WebAuthn security keys (FIDO2) and passkeys, with one-time recovery codes;
SMS is not offered.

Admins enforce MFA for the organization or chosen groups, set an enrollment grace period for new staff (0–30 days) during which each sign-in requires enrollment before content opens, may require phishing-resistant factors (security keys or passkeys) for admins, and set session length and idle timeout for web, desktop and mobile.
When MFA is enforced an email sign-in link alone never opens a session: the second factor is always required, and a stolen link fails without it.

A user who loses every factor recovers through a recovery code or through a help-desk admin (ADMIN-003) who verifies them and issues a single-use enrollment link that expires in 24 hours; every reset is audited and notifies the user.
Federated sign-ins rely on the IdP's MFA, which admins can require.
**Acceptance evidence:** Enforce MFA for everyone with a 0-day grace period.
An unenrolled staff member's next email-link sign-in is held at enrollment, enrolls a TOTP factor and then opens the library; a second user enrolls a passkey.
Replay a captured valid email link from another browser without the factor and be refused.
Require security keys for admins and prove an admin with only TOTP is refused the console.
Set a 1-hour session length and see a session end.
A user who has lost their factor is reset by a help-desk admin, enrolls again through the single-use link, and the link fails on second use and after 24 hours.
Admins with service-settings scope (ADMIN-003) set storage limits in bytes at two scopes.
**Per-user limits** cover a person's personal area.
There is an organization default and per-group limits.
A group limit overrides the organization default; a user in several limited groups gets the largest of those limits; a per-user override beats both.
The console shows each user's effective limit and the rule it came from.
**Per-space limits** have an organization default for spaces, inherited by every space unless an admin sets a per-space override;
SPACE-002 can set a different starting limit for new spaces.
**What counts:** a user's limit counts the current and all retained versions of items in their personal area plus their personal trash.
A space's limit counts its current and retained versions plus its trash, never charged to members.
Items shared with someone do not count against them.
Bytes stop counting only when an ERASE-001 erasure completes.
**Before saving** any new or lowered limit, the console lists every user and space already over it, with current usage, and requires confirmation.
Users, and the managers of a space, get an in-app and email warning at 90% of a limit.

**Over the limit**, these are refused with an error naming the limit's scope, the limit and the current usage: uploads, new versions, copies or moves into the over-limit area, sync-client uploads, editor saves (EDIT-001) and version restores that add bytes.
Viewing, preview, download, search, sharing, commenting, moving within the same scope, trashing and erasing keep working.
The browser shows the reason on the file and folder page.
The API returns `storage_limit_exceeded` with the scope, limit and usage.

How the macOS/Windows client shows a refusal in its tray and on each held file, keeping unsent changes queued and resuming them automatically, is SYNC-003; how the mobile app shows it on its upload queue is MOBILE-001.
**Freeing space:** in a personal area, the user trashes items and empties their own trash.
In a space, content managers trash items and space managers erase them under ERASE-001.
Admins can raise the limit.
Writes resume on the next request once usage is under the limit.
Every limit change is audited with before and after values.
**Acceptance evidence:** Set a group user limit and a space limit below current usage; before saving, the console lists the affected users and spaces with their usage, and saving needs confirmation.
Show that a group limit beats the organization default, and that a user in two limited groups gets the larger.
For the over-limit user, an upload is refused in the browser at 1440 and 390 and through the API with `storage_limit_exceeded`, each naming the limit; view, preview and download still work.
In the over-limit space, a content manager trashes content and usage does not drop until a space manager erases it under ERASE-001; writes then resume on the next request.
Inspect the 90% warning emails and the audit entries for each limit change.
The client tray and held-file display, with the queued upload completing without user action, is accepted under SYNC-003, and the mobile upload-queue display under MOBILE-001.
Transport, owner-selected storage and device caches use encryption with explicit installation/provider key custody, rotation and recovery procedures.
Provider credentials, link capabilities and signing keys remain secret, encrypted at rest and absent from source, served assets, product archives, logs and AI prompts.
Server-side current-session/origin checks cover every mutation; integrations use least scopes and revocation, and exported portable grants confer no login authority.
**Acceptance evidence:** Inspect public API, logs and archive output using a test canary credential, rotate/revoke a provider and device key, and retry old access.
Submit a cross-origin mutation, unauthenticated request and stale grant race; all fail closed while authorized originals remain recoverable under the documented key policy.
Separately deployed malware scanning and classification detect infected uploads, suspicious mass downloads/deletes and sensitive content.

Owners configure classification-based access, external sharing restrictions and quarantine/release roles, see reasons and false-positive handling, and can pause a device/token without destroying evidence.
Original bytes never bypass a pending quarantine via an alternate preview, range or sync door.

Mass-activity alerts have stated defaults that admins with security scope (ADMIN-003) tune per organization and group: one account, device or token downloading more than **500 files or 5 GB**, or trashing or deleting more than **200 items**, within **10 minutes**.
The default alerts admins; admins can also choose to pause the account's downloads or the device/token at the threshold.
Every threshold change is audited with before and after values.
The adopted policy requires explicit owner confirmation before processing and owner-only configuration of reader and reviewer groups.
A release needs a recorded reason and either the owner or a selected reviewer with current security scope over the uploader.
Ordinary content roles still apply.
Pending or failed verdicts and sensitive external sharing deny access.
Processing admits originals up to 1 GiB; larger originals stay quarantined.
Future doors in SYNC-001, MOBILE-001, CONNECT-001, CONNECT-002, CONNECT-008, CONNECT-009 and CONNECT-010 inherit these gates before shipping.
**Acceptance evidence:** Submit a standard harmless malware-test specimen and a labeled sensitive document, simulate a burst through a test client and inspect quarantine/alert history.
With the defaults, download 501 files in 10 minutes from one account and see the alert; trash 199 items and see none.
Lower a group's download threshold to 100 files with pause on and see the 101st download in the window refused while the alert names the rule.
Try all preview/download/link/device doors, release only as an authorized reviewer and prove policy changes do not erase originals or silently expand access.

The SYNC-001/006 clients watch outgoing changes for mass encryption or corruption: bursts of rewrites whose content entropy jumps toward random, file signatures that no longer match their extensions, mass renames to new extensions and known ransom-note files.
On detection the client pauses upload from that device before the server's current versions change, keeps downloading paused for affected folders, and holds the suspect changes locally.
The same detection runs server-side on public API and browser uploads, pausing the token or session.
The user and admins with security scope (ADMIN-003) are alerted at once in the client, by email and in the admin console, which names the device, account, first detection time and affected files.

One action restores every affected file to its last version before the incident (or a chosen point under RECOVER-001), keeps the suspect versions as quarantined history, and leaves later legitimate edits by other devices untouched; a false positive is released with one action and uploads resume.
The device stays paused until a user or admin resumes it.
**Acceptance evidence:** From a test client, rewrite 500 synced files with high-entropy content in under a minute.
Upload pauses before any server current-version ID changes; the client, email and admin console show the event with device and file list.
While paused, another device's legitimate edit to a different file syncs normally.
Run the one-action restore and verify every affected file's current version and SHA-256 equals its last pre-incident version, with the 500 suspect versions retained as quarantined history.
Repeat through the public API with a token and see the token paused.
Release a deliberate false positive and see uploads resume with no loss.
Owners configure retention classes, holds and erasure conflicts with a qualified immutable archive/eDiscovery service such as Amazon S3 Object Lock and Microsoft Purview.
Export includes scoped originals, versions, chain of custody and activity; hold status names the provider’s acknowledgment, policy and retained scope.
Chest does not call ordinary R2 storage certified WORM or invent legal sufficiency.
**Acceptance evidence:** Place a test project on provider-confirmed hold, request deletion, export a discovery package and reconcile hashes, versions and audit at the provider.
Attempt deletion before release; show the hold/refusal and then an authorized release/erasure with the provider outcome.
A searchable, exportable audit
attributes reads/downloads, sharing/admin mutations, device actions and every automation/provider attempt to actor, exact version, authority and outcome.
Failed/uncertain/crashed jobs retain durable outcomes and cannot disappear on restart or become success by timeout.
Pagination/export includes all retained history beyond UI limits;
audit payloads omit secrets
and anonymize erased identities without deleting the action record.

**File activity for collaborators:** each file's activity panel shows everyone with viewer access or above its edits, versions, comments, moves and sharing changes, and shows people who can edit it (contributor, file editor and above) which colleagues viewed it and when, as Drive's activity dashboard does.
Admins turn view history on or off for the organization or a group, and each user can hide their own views; guests' and link visitors' views appear only as counts unless the viewer is a manager.
The panel is filtered by current access and never reveals a viewer of an item the requester cannot see.
**Acceptance evidence:** Create success, refusal, provider failure and interrupted execution through public doors, restart and inspect/export more events than one UI page.
Reconcile action/version IDs and outcomes and then erase an actor without losing the fact of their actions or exposing personal/secret fields.
On a space file, two colleagues view it; a contributor sees both names and times in the file's activity panel and a viewer sees edits but no view history.
A colleague who hides their views disappears from the list, and turning view history off for the group removes it from the panel.

Authorized permanent erasure removes selected originals, all versions, derived text/thumbnails/embeddings, guest/link authority, import staging/custody and affected backup copies under disclosed provider retention.
It revokes identities and credentials where requested, writes a durable per-store receipt and source erasure fence, and preserves a minimized anonymized action audit.
Legal holds produce explicit refusal/pending provider outcomes.
Offline historical copies cannot be recalled: restores must apply the later source journal or disclose the inability to know later erasures.

**Acceptance evidence:** Through an owner erasure workflow remove a populated file and a staff identity, inspect each storage/index/import/backup target and audit anonymization, restart and attempt search/download and restore of an older archive with the later erasure journal.
Refuse resurrection; show an unreachable backup or held object as pending rather than complete.

Browser, native and admin paths expose loading, empty, failed and permission-denied states in words, preserve unfinished input and support keyboard/screen-reader operation with WCAG 2.2 AA as a tested target.
Operators see health and stale/background jobs, configured US time zones, capacity, backup failures and measured deployment limits.
The availability target, durability of originals and incident notices are OPS-002.
fragments.note: pointer to the availability clause, whose parts OPS-002.1 to OPS-002.3 now stand alone

fragments.text: Hosted mail, clients, processing and storage use named real accounts and reproducible install/update steps; no demo or provider stub counts as production acceptance.

**Acceptance evidence:** Use realistic nested project data through store/open/share/search/recover at 1440 and 390, keyboard and a screen reader; disconnect each service and recover without fake success or lost edits.
Install the documented stack in an owner test account and record its measured limits and actionable health signals; the SCALE-001 run supplies the size and timings.

Chest serves a **reference installation** of 150 users, 300 synced devices, 10 TB of current originals plus version history, 2,000,000 items in total, a largest space of 500,000 items with 100 nested folder levels and 600 direct members, and a largest folder of 20,000 direct children.
When a buyer's MIGRATE-001 inventory is larger in any dimension, acceptance runs at that inventory plus 25% growth headroom instead.

At that size, measured at the 95th percentile from a US region on a 100 Mbps connection: the first page of a folder listing returns within 1 second and a 20,000-child folder scrolls without a full reload; full-text search across the user's accessible items returns first results within 2 seconds; a permission change is enforced on the next request through every door; a device offline for 7 days catches up on 10,000 remote changes within 15 minutes; a new device's initial on-demand enumeration of a 500,000-item space completes within 30 minutes without hydrating file bytes.
Measured figures are published in the operator console, and a deployment that misses a target reports it as a failing health check rather than silently degrading.
**Acceptance evidence:** Generate the reference installation (or the buyer's inventory plus 25%) with a seeded generator that records item, byte, depth, member and device counts.
Run a fixed script of folder listings, deep-path opens, 50 search queries, a revocation and an offline-device catch-up, and publish the counts and p50/p95 timings for each against the targets above.
Revoke a group during the run and prove the next request through list, search, download and sync is refused.
Rerun against a buyer's MIGRATE-001 inventory and show the size used.
**Availability:** Chest targets **99.9% monthly availability**, separately for each door: web, API, sync (the client service endpoint) and links (SHARE-001–003).
External probes from at least two US regions exercise each door every minute with a real signed-in or link request, not just a health ping.
A minute counts as down for a door when probes from two regions fail it.
Planned maintenance is announced at least 72 hours ahead in the incident notice and counts as downtime.
The operator console publishes each door's monthly percentage and minute history against the target, and a month heading below target raises a failing health check and an admin alert.
On a hosted installation, service credits are set by the operator's service terms; the target and how it is measured are fixed here.

**Durability:** every original version is held as at least **two independent copies in separate failure domains**, a primary object store such as Cloudflare R2 plus a copy with a different provider or region such as Amazon S3.
The second copy is written within 15 minutes of admission, and any admitted version still waiting for it is shown in the console.
A **scrub** re-reads every stored copy at least every 30 days and checks its SHA-256 against the checksum recorded at admission (CHEST-03).
A mismatched or missing copy is repaired from a verified good copy, with an audit entry.
If no good copy exists, the file is shown as damaged to its owner and admins and is never served as intact.
A monthly durability report gives the objects and bytes verified, mismatches found, repairs made and anything unrecoverable.
RECOVER-002 backups are additional to these copies.
**Incident status:** automated probes open an incident, and operators open or update one.
It names the affected doors, start time and updates.
A banner appears in the browser, the desktop client tray, the mobile app and the admin console within 2 minutes of automated detection, and admins get an email.
The status is also published on a status page served independently of the main application.
Clearing the incident removes the banners and records its duration against the availability figures.
A client that cannot reach Chest shows "Chest unreachable" with its last successful contact (SYNC-003), distinct from a local network failure where the client can tell.
**Acceptance evidence:** Run the probes for 30 days
against the SCALE-001 reference installation
fragments.note: "against the SCALE-001 reference installation": availability does not need the reference size (RL-20)

fragments.text: and publish each door's availability and minute history against the 99.9% target.
Take one door down for a measured interval and see it counted.
Corrupt one stored copy of an original and delete the second copy of another: the next scrub detects both, repairs each from its good copy, and records audit entries and the durability report.
Make one object unrecoverable in both copies and see it shown as damaged, never served.

Stop the API: an incident opens automatically, the banner shows in the browser at 1440 and 390, the macOS and Windows clients and both mobile apps within 2 minutes, the independent status page reports it and admins receive the email.
Restore the API and see the banners clear and the duration recorded.
Chest is free, open-source software.
The whole product, every capability in this contract, ships as MIT-licensed source in this repository, with the license text at the repository root and in every release.
Chest has no license key, seat count, user cap, paid edition, trial expiry or feature gate, and it never charges for or meters people, storage or features.

Costs that come from the owner's own providers (hosting, storage, mail, a Collabora Online subscription or Microsoft 365 licenses under EDIT-001, AI spend under AGENT-007) belong to those providers and are never a Chest charge; showing them in USD with each provider named is ADMIN-002's provider-only cost view.
Bundled third-party components keep their own licenses: every production dependency, direct and transitive, is listed with its license in each release.

**Acceptance evidence:** Build a release from a fresh clone: the MIT license text is at its root, and a third-party license list names every production dependency, direct and transitive, with its version and license.

Install it, invite 150 staff (the SCALE-001 reference user count) and use every delivered capability through the browser, the API and the clients: no license key, payment, seat prompt, user cap or feature lock appears, and a source scan of the release finds no license-key, seat-limit or paywall check.
The cost view that lists only provider costs, each labeled with its provider, is accepted under ADMIN-002.
The owner runs Chest on infrastructure they control, with no Chest-operated service in the path, on any of three targets:
**Their own computer** (macOS, Linux, or Windows with WSL2), with one line, `npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-chest`, which clones, installs, sets up a local owner and starts Chest;
`rer dev` inside the checkout starts it again.
**Their own server**: a Linux host or VM they operate, on premises or rented, serving staff over HTTPS on the owner's domain with the owner's mail provider and object storage.
**Their own cloud account**:
Cloudflare, as `deploy.json` describes.
Every target keeps original bytes and metadata in owner-controlled storage and needs no account other than the owner's chosen providers.
The owner moves an installation between targets by CHEST-12 export and restore without loss.
A computer install says when other devices cannot reach it, rather than implying team availability.
Install, update and rollback steps are reproducible from the documentation (OPS-001, RECOVER-002).
**Acceptance evidence:** From a fresh clone on macOS and on Ubuntu LTS, run the five documented commands and reach the signed-in owner library in the browser.
On a Linux VM the owner controls, install Chest with the documented server steps and sign in from a second computer over HTTPS on the owner's domain.
Invite a staff member whose email link arrives through the owner's mail provider, then upload, share and download a file whose bytes are in the owner's storage.
Deploy the same release to the owner's Cloudflare account.
Export the server install with `rer export`, restore it into the cloud install with `rer import`, and reconcile every original's SHA-256 and every record (CHEST-12).
Block outbound access to every Run Edit Run host and see each running install keep serving staff.
Every source adapter inventories all files/folders, owners, principals, versions, timestamps, comments, links and unsupported records with counts/bytes/hashes and a reason for each gap.

Open review work is live state, not history: every adapter inventories, per file, comments, replies, open and resolved threads, assigned comments or tasks and pending suggestions or tracked changes, and moves whatever the source exposes through its API or export into EDIT-003 threads, tasks and tracked changes under the same thread, author, assignee, suggestion, notification and reconciliation rules that MIGRATE-002 states for Google Drive.
Anything a source cannot expose is a named per-file gap in the migration report, never a silent drop.
The owner previews identity/permission mappings, approves the exact plan and runs resumable idempotent batches plus a delta catch-up before cutover.
Unmapped rights fail closed; imported approvals remain source history.
Links inside migrated content are rewritten to the migrated items, and old vendor URLs pasted from mail, calendars or other systems resolve through a staff resolver (MIGRATE-007).
Chest never claims an ability to own the vendors' domains; redirects on those domains remain source-controlled.
A cutover manifest tracks replacement URLs and collaborator tests; rollback retains source read access and an independent archive.

**Acceptance evidence:** Through the migration wizard, inventory a representative source, change the source after preview, reject stale plans, resume an interrupted batch and reconcile every item and version.

Approve delta/cutover, test internal and external collaborators and old-to-new links (rewritten links and the resolver, under MIGRATE-007), then undo untouched work and preserve native edits as conflicts.

The inventory and the migration report give per-file counts of comments, replies, open, resolved and assigned items and pending suggestions in the source and in Chest, every difference carries a reason, and no notification is sent for migrated review work during any batch or delta.

Import Google Drive personal/shared drives using authorized APIs/export, preserving folder IDs/mapping, team ownership, file and revision bytes, shortcuts, native Google types and explicit user/group/domain ACLs.
Reconcile imported approvals and unavailable revisions as sourced history/gaps; open review work moves as live review state under the block below.
Google conversion fidelity and the MIGRATE-007 link rewrite and unresolved-link report require owner acceptance before declaring Drive replaced.
The adapter also carries:
fragments.note: list heading ("The adapter also carries:"); its items are MIGRATE-002.2-.4

fragments.text: **Drive labels:** each label becomes a CHEST-02 type and each field a typed field (text, number, date, selection with its options, user), with applied values copied per file and the label/field IDs kept as provenance; badged labels and disabled options are inventoried, and any field type without an equivalent is a named gap.
**Shared-drive roles:** Manager, Content manager, Contributor, Commenter and Viewer map one-to-one to the ROLE-001 manager, content manager, contributor, commenter and viewer roles;

My Drive file roles Editor/Commenter/Viewer map to file editor/commenter/viewer; the shared-drive "allow viewers and commenters to download" and "sharing outside the drive" settings map to the ROLE-001 no-download and POLICY-001 space overrides.
No mapping widens a role.

**Google Vault:** retention rules and holds covering migrating accounts, shared drives or files are inventoried from the Vault API with matter, scope and dates; content under a hold or a retention rule migrates only after the owner acknowledges a receiving GOVERN-001 policy for it, and the migration report lists each one with its receiving policy.

**Externally owned files:** files owned outside the domain that staff rely on (Shared with me, shortcuts to them and externally owned items in shared drives) are inventoried with owner, sharing and the staff who use them.
For each, the owner chooses to copy it in with the source owner's consent recorded, keep it as a labeled external link, or request transfer from the source owner; none is silently copied or dropped.

**Open review work (comments, action items and suggestions):** on every migrated file with comments, whether a native Doc, Sheet or Slides file, a Drive-hosted Office file, or a PDF or image commented in Drive's preview, the review work open on cutover day arrives as live EDIT-003 review state, not a read-only record:

**Threads:** each Drive comment not marked deleted becomes one EDIT-003 thread on the migrated file, with its replies in order, its original created and modified times and its Drive comment and reply IDs kept as provenance ("migrated from Google Drive").
It is open if it was open and resolved if it was resolved, following the resolve and reopen actions recorded in its replies.
It is anchored to the quoted text, cell, slide, or PDF or image page and region, located from the export's comment ranges and the API's `anchor` and `quotedFileContent`.
When neither locates it in the migrated version, the thread is flagged "anchor not found", attached to the file with its quoted text kept, and listed in the report.
Deleted comments are counted, not migrated.
**Authors:** the Drive API does not return comment authors' email addresses or permission IDs, so Chest matches each author by evidence, in this order:
(1) for domain users, the migration lists each file's comments as each migrating user under its domain-wide delegation, and the API marks that user's own comments and replies with `me`;
(2) the Drive Activity API's comment actors, resolved to directory users through the Admin SDK Directory API;

(3) for anyone left, the author's display name matched against the file's permission list, the domain directory and existing SHARE-005 guests, which is only a proposal, applied once the owner confirms it in the MIGRATE-001 mapping preview.

Each comment and reply is attributed to the matched Chest identity, or to a SHARE-005 guest identity carrying an external author's email, created without access unless the file's migrated permissions grant it.
An author who cannot be matched, including a deleted user, is shown as "Former collaborator (name as in source)", is never attributed to another person and is listed in the report.
EDIT-001's `author_mismatch` rule applies to the import: no migrated comment, reply or tracked change is written under a guessed author.
**Mentions and action items:** the API's `mentionedEmailAddresses` become EDIT-003 mentions of the mapped people, and a mention grants no access.
An assigned comment keeps its assignee from `assigneeEmailAddress` and becomes an open task in that person's EDIT-003 and FOLLOW-001 task lists, keeping its source age.

If the assignee was not migrated or cannot open the migrated file, no access is granted: the report names the assignee and the reason, the task goes to the file's owner (for a space file, the space's managers), and the owner is offered EDIT-001's one-step grant.
**Suggestions:** when a Doc is converted to DOCX or ODT, each pending Suggesting-mode edit becomes a tracked change in Collabora Online, attributed under the same author rule.
The Docs API's suggestion IDs reconcile the export's tracked changes so that none is dropped or duplicated.
A contributor accepts or rejects each one as an EDIT-001 decision version.
**Files kept native:** when a Doc, Sheet or Slides file stays native under EDIT-002, its comments and suggestions stay in Google.
Chest shows them on the file page and in the apps as provider-held, with counts and a link to open them in Google, creates no duplicate threads and counts them as provider-held in the report.
Converting such a file later under EDIT-002 applies this block at conversion time.
**No notifications on move-in:** the migration and every delta pass send no mention, assignment, reply or reminder notification.
A delta pass carries the comments, replies, resolves, reopens and reassignments made in Google since the previous pass, idempotently by source ID, with no duplicate thread.
FOLLOW-001 reminders for migrated tasks start one full reminder interval after cutover, never on cutover day.
The owner may instead choose one summary email per assignee at cutover listing their moved tasks; it is off by default.

**Reconciliation:** the migration report counts, per file, comments, replies, open, resolved and assigned items and pending suggestions in the source and in Chest, and lists every difference with its reason (author not matched, anchor not found, assignee without access, provider-held, deleted in source).
Drive is not declared replaced while any difference lacks a reason.

**Acceptance evidence:** Migrate a real test Workspace with Shared Drives, a departed owner, native Docs/Sheets/Slides, shortcuts, nested restricted folders and historical versions, plus: a labeled file with a date field and a selection field; a shared drive with one member at each of the five roles and download-restricted viewers; a Vault hold and a retention rule over one shared drive; and an externally owned file shared into a shared drive and another in a staff member's Shared with me.

Compare inventory, byte hashes, exported/native fidelity, principals and links; verify the label values as typed fields, run the ROLE-001 role tests against each migrated member, see the held content blocked until a GOVERN-001 policy is acknowledged, and see both external files reconciled by the chosen option or reported as named gaps requiring owner sign-off.
Prove an external collaborator can use the replacement without access to forbidden folders.
Include the MIGRATE-007 link fixtures in the same tenant and pass that clause's acceptance.

Seed the same tenant with open review work: a Doc with three open threads, one of them with two replies and one assigned to staff member B; a resolved thread; two pending suggestions by staff member C; a comment by an external collaborator; a comment by a departed, deleted user; a Sheet with a cell comment; and a PDF with a region comment made in Drive's preview.
Migrate with the Doc converted to DOCX:
The DOCX opens in Collabora Online with the three open threads and the resolved thread in their states, anchored to their text.
On the file page and in the iOS and Android apps they are EDIT-003 threads with their original timestamps, attributed to the mapped Chest users.
The external comment carries the guest's email, and the departed user's comment shows as "Former collaborator (name as in source)".
B finds the assigned comment in their task list.
The notification log shows nothing sent to anyone during the migration or the delta pass, and no reminder on cutover day.
C's two suggestions are tracked changes attributed to C.
A contributor accepts one and rejects the other, and each decision is an EDIT-001 decision version.
The Sheet's cell comment and the PDF's region comment are EDIT-003 threads on the right cell and on the right page and region.
Add a reply and resolve a thread in Google, run the delta pass, and see each arrive once, with no notification.
The report's per-file counts match the source.

An injected author with no match shows as a former collaborator and is listed with its reason, never as another person; an injected comment whose quoted text was removed is flagged "anchor not found" with its quoted text kept; an assignment to a user who cannot open the file goes to the file's owner and is listed, with no access granted.
Repeat with the Doc kept native under EDIT-002: its comments stay in Google, Chest reports them as provider-held with counts and a link, and no thread is duplicated.

Import member folders and team spaces through Dropbox APIs/export with revisions, deleted-file history where available, metadata, shared-folder membership and external links mapped under current Chest policy.
Preserve distinct file IDs for equal hashes, account for selective-sync placeholders and report missing revision/transfer history explicitly.

File comments move as EDIT-003 threads under the MIGRATE-001 open-review-work rules wherever the Dropbox API or export exposes them; where it exposes none for a file, the report names that file's comments as a gap.

**Acceptance evidence:** Migrate a real Dropbox Business test team containing a team folder, personal folder, revisions, deleted file and expiring links, plus a file with an open comment thread: it arrives as an attributed EDIT-003 thread with no notification sent, or is listed in the report as a named gap.
Reconcile every source item/version and rights, perform a delta import, reissue controlled links and validate recipient workflows before cutover.
Import Box folders, original/version bytes, metadata templates, collaborators, shared links and comments/tasks through authorized APIs/export.
Preserve source legal-hold/retention/approval provenance separately and require an acknowledged receiving governance policy where relevant; never turn a source role into broader Chest rights.

Box comments become EDIT-003 threads, and Box tasks become EDIT-003 tasks with their assignees, due dates and completion state, under the MIGRATE-001 open-review-work rules, with no notification on move-in.

**Acceptance evidence:** Migrate a real Box test space with custom metadata, a limited collaborator, versioned file and shared link, plus a file with a comment thread and an open task assigned to a collaborator: the thread arrives attributed, and the task is in the assignee's list with its due date, with no notification sent.
Reconcile counts/hash/history and rights, report provider-held or unavailable items, test a guest and reconcile signed-off cutover/rollback.

Import OneDrive for Business and SharePoint document libraries through Microsoft Graph/export, preserving sites/library folder structure, originals/revisions, owners, groups, unique item permissions, metadata/content types and sharing-link mappings.
Pages/lists and suite-specific workflows are inventoried with explicit handoff rather than silently called files or dropped.

Comments stored in Office files become EDIT-003 threads under the MIGRATE-001 open-review-work rules, with authors matched from the Microsoft Entra ID identity Office records on each comment, through Graph, and confirmed in the mapping preview.

**Acceptance evidence:** Migrate a real Microsoft 365 test tenant with a SharePoint library, OneDrive user, restricted subfolder, versions and guest link, plus a DOCX with an open and a resolved comment by different users, which arrive as EDIT-003 threads attributed to the mapped people, in their states, with no notification sent.
Reconcile records/bytes/ACLs and unsupported pages/workflows, run a delta, offboard the source owner and validate the replacement links as staff and guest.
Move Egnyte folders, LucidLink filespaces, Nextcloud/WebDAV libraries and SMB/NAS trees through documented APIs or mounted originals with a source manifest.
Preserve names, bytes, times, rights and available history and report unavailable streamed ranges, encrypted content or vendor-only data.
Hybrid cache and creative-workflow acceptance must succeed before retiring those source systems.

**Acceptance evidence:** Inventory a test filespace from each named challenger plus a NAS share, hydrate placeholders, migrate and reconcile hashes and rights; open a large creative file from the replacement mount and test a revoked collaborator.
Any unexportable history remains a named gap requiring owner sign-off.
**Source-to-Chest map:** every migration (MIGRATE-002–006) records a persistent map from each source ID (file, folder, shared drive or site, and revision where available) to its Chest stable ID.
The map is kept after cutover and included in CHEST-12 and RECOVER-002 archives.
**Rewriting:** during the job, and again in a final pass after the last delta, Chest rewrites source URLs that point at migrated items so they open the Chest items.
Covered URLs:
Google Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides and Forms file, folder and `open?id=` URLs, and shared-drive URLs;
Dropbox shared links and paths;
Box shared and web-app links;
OneDrive and SharePoint sharing links and paths.
Rewriting reaches inside:
DOCX, XLSX, PPTX and ODF files: hyperlinks, `HYPERLINK` formulas, linked objects and external workbook references;
Google Docs, Sheets and Slides, whether kept native under EDIT-002 or converted.
A Sheets `IMPORTRANGE` in a sheet kept native is pointed at the migrated target spreadsheet.
In a sheet converted to XLSX it becomes an external workbook link to the migrated file where the editor supports one; otherwise it is reported, with its cached values kept;
PDF link annotations;
Drive shortcuts and `.url`/`.webloc` files;
item descriptions.
A rewrite creates a new attributed "migration link rewrite" version, with the source bytes kept as the prior version, so hash reconciliation against the source still holds.

**Unresolved report:** every link not rewritten is listed with its file, location (page, sheet and cell, or slide), source URL, intended target and reason: excluded from the migration, not found, no access, externally owned, unsupported format or encrypted.
The report also counts every link rewritten, by source vendor and by where it was found, and the migration summary shows that total.
The owner accepts the report before cutover.

**Resolver:** a staff-only resolver page and API, also used by the CONNECT-008 add-ins and Slack/Teams unfurls (CONNECT-001/002), turns an old source URL pasted from an email, calendar invite or other system into the migrated item.
A user with current access gets the item.
A user without access gets Request access (SHARE-004) and never sees the title.
An unmigrated URL is reported as not migrated.
Guests and signed-out browsers are refused.
Historical mail and calendar content are not rewritten in place, because the source vendor controls them; the resolver covers them.
**Acceptance evidence:** The MIGRATE-002 test tenant includes:
a Doc linking to a Sheet in another shared drive;
a Sheet with `IMPORTRANGE`, kept native in one run and converted to XLSX in another;
a PPTX and a PDF with Drive links;
a Drive shortcut and a `.url` file;
a link to a file excluded from the migration.
After migration, every link except the excluded one opens the matching Chest item, and each rewritten file's prior version still matches the source hash.
The excluded link appears in the unresolved report with file, location, target and reason, and the summary's rewritten-link count equals the rewritten fixtures, per vendor.
Migrate a newly linked file in a delta and see the final pass rewrite its link.
An old Drive URL pasted into the resolver opens the item for a member, shows Request access without the title to a non-member, and is refused for a guest.
Run an equivalent Dropbox, Box and SharePoint link fixture through MIGRATE-003–005.
A scoped Slack app finds Chest files, shares policy-checked links and delivers subscribed comments, requests and review notifications in approved channels/DMs.
Searches and link previews use the requesting user’s current access; channel membership is not a library grant.
Admins control installation, scopes and revocation.
**Acceptance evidence:** Connect a real Slack test workspace, search/share as two users with different rights, change a folder grant and inspect channel unfurls/notifications.
Revoke the app and prove it can no longer search/send; existing Chest links still enforce their own audience.
A Microsoft Teams app supports file search/pick/open, controlled links and collaboration notifications under Entra-linked user identity and current Chest grants.
Channel/private-chat content does not inherit broad storage access; tenant admins can restrict and revoke the app.
**Acceptance evidence:** Connect a real Teams test tenant, share a restricted file into a mixed-membership channel, open/edit as an authorized user and deny another.
Revoke a group/app and verify search, cards, previews and queued notifications stop exposing content.

Salesforce account/contact/opportunity records and HubSpot company/contact/deal records link to scoped Chest folders and versions through a Salesforce app and a HubSpot app (a CRM record card listing the linked folder's files); authorized users file arrivals and see current approved content without duplicating CRM ownership.
Mapping changes retain provenance and never grant every CRM user Chest access.

**Acceptance evidence:** Connect a Salesforce test org, attach a file to an opportunity, replace/approve it, change record/folder access and delete the CRM link; the original and provenance remain while unauthorized CRM users see no file content.
Repeat with a HubSpot test portal on a deal: the record card lists the linked folder's files for a user with Chest access and shows none to a HubSpot user without it.
Send a human-selected exact version to Docusign, track envelope state and receive signed originals plus completion evidence as new immutable linked versions.
Verify callback authenticity, reconcile uncertain submissions and deduplicate repeated callbacks;
Chest approval is distinct from legal signature validity.
Built-in signing that needs no third-party account is SIGN-001; this clause serves firms that standardize on Docusign or need its notarization and qualified signatures.
**Acceptance evidence:** Send an approved test agreement in a Docusign sandbox, complete and decline envelopes, replay a signed callback and simulate an uncertain send.
Retain signed bytes/certificate, verify no duplicate envelope/version and never mark the pending source file signed on provider acknowledgment alone.

Zoom integration lets authorized meeting participants pick permitted Chest files, share controlled links and file authorized cloud recordings/transcripts into a selected folder with source consent/provenance.
A meeting invitation alone grants no file access; recording retention follows configured owner policy.
Google Meet recordings, transcripts and notes are filed the same way under CONNECT-010.
**Acceptance evidence:** In a Zoom test account, share a restricted deck with a guest and file an authorized recording/transcript after the meeting.
Deny an unrelated participant and a revoked integration, inspect exact version/provenance and ensure a canceled recording job reports its real state.
Gmail/Google Workspace and Microsoft Outlook/Exchange Online connectors ingest only owner-approved mailboxes, labels/folders, senders and attachments into selected Chest destinations.
Authorized Salesforce/Slack/Teams/Zoom app arrivals use the same provenance and deduplication rules.
Reply/forward or external collection messages require a preview or narrowly granted standing recipient/cadence policy; revocation stops subsequent reads and sends.

**Acceptance evidence:** Connect real test Gmail and Microsoft 365 mailboxes, ingest an attachment once despite duplicate delivery, inspect source message/version provenance and reject a disallowed folder/sender.
Revoke one source and verify queued jobs and sends stop at the authorization boundary.
Documented file/folder/version/search/share/request APIs and an MCP server provide user/agent-scoped access, pagination, stable IDs, idempotent mutations and signed event delivery.
Grants name allowed resources/actions and budgets; secrets are installation-local.

A documented, embeddable Chest file picker (a JavaScript component with an OAuth grant flow) lets third-party web apps offer "attach from Chest" under the user's current access, as they offer Drive's picker; it returns stable IDs and policy-checked links only.
Webhook consumers deduplicate event IDs, see delivery failure/uncertainty and control replay; imported events do not send automatically.

**Third-party app control:** an admin with sharing and security policy scope (ADMIN-003) sets, for the organization or named groups, whether staff may authorize any app, only allowlisted apps, or none.
Each app (OAuth client, MCP agent, picker origin, or the CONNECT-009 Zapier and Make apps) can be trusted, limited to read-only scopes, or blocked.
Staff cannot authorize an app the policy does not allow; the consent screen names the policy.
Blocking an app or tightening the policy revokes its existing grants on the next request.
The console lists every authorized app with its users, scopes and last use, and each policy change is audited.
**Acceptance evidence:** Authorize a third-party test client and MCP agent for one folder, exercise paginated reads and idempotent upload, then attempt another folder and permission expansion.
Revoke the grant mid-job, fail a signed webhook and inspect its durable outcome/manual replay without duplicated product mutations.

Embed the file picker in a test web app: a user picks an accessible file and the app receives its stable ID and a link; a file the user cannot open never appears, and a revoked picker grant fails the next pick.

Set the policy to allowlist only: a staff member's attempt to authorize an app off the list is refused naming the policy, an app limited to read-only cannot upload, and blocking an already authorized app refuses its next call; the console lists each app with its users and scopes.

A Google Workspace add-on for Gmail and a Microsoft 365 add-in for Outlook (web, Windows, Mac and mobile) let each user, under their own Chest identity: pick a Chest file or folder while composing and insert it as a link at a chosen role; have any attachment over a set size (default 25 MB) turned into a SHARE-003 transfer link automatically; and save an incoming attachment, or the whole message as EML, to a Chest folder they choose.

Before sending, the add-in checks every recipient against each inserted item's current access and warns naming who cannot open it, offering a one-step grant at viewer or commenter that POLICY-001 permits (or explaining the refusal); the user can also send without granting.
Saves are idempotent per message and attachment, carry the message ID, sender and date as provenance, and are audited.
Admins install, scope and revoke the add-ins for the organization; the admin intake pipeline remains CONNECT-006.

**Acceptance evidence:** In real Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 test tenants, insert a restricted file into a message to an allowlisted external recipient; see the warning naming them, grant viewer in one step, send, and find the grant and audit entry; repeat to a non-allowlisted recipient and see the grant refused with the policy named.
Attach a 200 MB file and see it replaced by a transfer link that the recipient downloads.
Save the same attachment twice from Gmail and from Outlook and find one Chest file each with message provenance.
Revoke the add-in and see the next insert and save refused.
Published Zapier and Make apps let non-developers automate Chest without code, authorized through a CONNECT-007 grant naming the allowed spaces/folders and actions.
Triggers: new file, new file in folder (including subfolders by option), updated file (new version), new folder, file moved or trashed, new file-request submission (SHARE-002) and new comment.

Actions: upload file, create folder, move, copy, rename, share with a person or create a link (POLICY-001 enforced), remove permission, update typed metadata, find file or folder by path or search, and download file content for a later step.
Triggers deliver each event once with a stable event ID; actions are idempotent on a caller key.
Revoking or narrowing the grant stops triggers and refuses actions on the next call, and each Zap/scenario run appears in the audit under the grant.

**Acceptance evidence:** In real Zapier and Make test accounts, connect Chest with a grant for one folder and build "new file in folder → move to a subfolder and share with a colleague"; drop a file in and see it moved and shared once, with audit entries under the grant.
Replay the trigger and see no duplicate move.
Point an action at a folder outside the grant and see it refused; attempt a public link with public links off under POLICY-001 and see the policy refusal.
Revoke the grant and see the next trigger stop and the next action fail.

Organizations that keep Google Workspace for mail and meetings get Chest as the file store behind Google Meet, Google Calendar, Google Chat and Google Forms, as CONNECT-001/002/005 do for Slack, Teams and Zoom and CONNECT-008 does for Gmail.

A super admin or an admin with service-settings scope (ADMIN-003) authorizes one Workspace connection through a Google Workspace Marketplace install with the named Meet, Calendar, Chat, Forms and Drive scopes, chooses which organizers, form owners or groups it covers, and installs, scopes and revokes each of the four parts separately.
**Meet recordings, transcripts and notes.** For each covered organizer, every Meet recording, transcript and Gemini "take notes for me" document is filed **once** into a mapped Chest folder.

The folder is the one the event is linked to through the Calendar add-on, or one set by an admin rule per calendar or group; otherwise it is a "Meet recordings" folder in the organizer's personal area.
Chest detects new artifacts from Workspace event notifications, with a reconciliation sweep at least hourly.
Both are keyed on the conference record and artifact ID, so a replayed event or the sweep never files twice.
Each filed file carries provenance: meeting code, conference record ID, organizer, start and end times, Calendar event ID and title, and the source Drive file ID.
Notes and transcripts are filed as native Google files under EDIT-002 or converted to DOCX, following the organization's EDIT-002 choice.
**Access:** the organizer becomes file editor.

Attendees whom Meet would have given access, under the Workspace recording-sharing setting, get viewer as named grants: internal attendees as staff, and external attendees as SHARE-005 guests only where POLICY-001 allows their domain.
Anyone POLICY-001 excludes is listed in the filing report as not granted.
Access is never widened beyond Meet's audience and the destination folder's own members.

**Source copy:** the admin chooses whether the Drive copy is kept or moved to Drive trash once the Chest copy's SHA-256 matches the downloaded original; removal never happens before that check and is audited.
A filing refused by QUOTA-001 or POLICY-001 keeps the Drive copy and is reported to the organizer and admins with the reason, never silently dropped.
Recordings already in Drive before cutover move under MIGRATE-002, keyed on the same artifact IDs so they are never filed twice.

**Calendar add-on.** A Google Workspace add-on for Google Calendar on the web lets a user attach a Chest file or folder to an event as a link at a chosen role, and link the event to a Chest folder for its Meet files.
When the event is saved, the add-on checks each guest against each attached item's current access, as CONNECT-008 checks recipients.
It names the guests who cannot open an item and offers a one-step viewer or commenter grant that POLICY-001 permits, or explains the refusal; the user can also save without granting.
Guests added later are checked at the next save through the add-on.
A guest who gets the invitation some other way, such as by forwarding, gains nothing and sees Request access (SHARE-004).
**Chat app.** A Google Chat app for spaces and direct messages, on the web and in the Chat mobile apps, gives the CONNECT-001 behaviors:
search Chest and share policy-checked links, with results limited to the requesting user's current access;
shared-link cards that show the title and a preview only when every member of the space or DM can open the item.
Otherwise the card shows neither, and any member who presses Preview gets a dialog rendered under their own current access: the preview if they have access, Request access without the title if not;
a private prompt to the sharer, visible only to them, naming members who lack access and offering a one-step grant that POLICY-001 permits;
subscribed notifications (comments, access requests, review requests, file-request arrivals) in chosen spaces or DMs under FOLLOW-001.
Membership of a Chat space is never a library grant.

**Forms file uploads.** For each form owned by a covered user, files submitted through a file-upload question are filed **once** into a Chest folder the form owner maps to that form, or a "Form uploads" folder in their personal area.
Filing is keyed on form ID, response ID and file ID, detected from Forms response notifications with an hourly reconciliation sweep.
Each file carries provenance: form ID and title, question, response ID, submission time, the respondent's email where the form collects it, and the source Drive file ID.
The form owner becomes file editor and the folder's members keep their access.
Respondents gain no access.
The same source-copy choice, SHA-256 check, QUOTA-001 and POLICY-001 refusals and reporting apply as for Meet files.
The form's responses spreadsheet stays a Google Sheet in the form owner's Drive:
Chest links it from the form's Chest folder, opens it under EDIT-002 and copies no response rows.
Every filing, attachment check, grant and refusal is audited with the Workspace actor.
Revoking one part, or the whole connection, refuses the next filing, attachment check, share or search.
