Files already filed keep their Chest permissions.
**Acceptance evidence:** In a real Google Workspace test tenant with the connection covering one group:

A group member schedules an event linked through the Calendar add-on to a restricted team-space folder, with one internal attendee and one external attendee from an allowlisted domain, and records the Meet with transcript and notes on.
The recording, transcript and notes document each appear once in the folder with meeting code, organizer, event ID and source Drive file ID.
The internal attendee opens them, the external attendee opens them as a guest viewer, and a staff member who was not invited and has no folder access gets 403.
Replay the Workspace event notification and run the reconciliation sweep: there is no duplicate.
With "remove source after verification" on, the Drive copy goes to Drive trash only after the SHA-256 check passes.
With the destination over its QUOTA-001 limit, the filing is refused with `storage_limit_exceeded`, the organizer and an admin are told, and the Drive copy is kept.
An organizer outside the covered group has nothing filed.
Through the Calendar add-on, attach a restricted Chest file to an event with one guest who has access and one who doesn't.
On save, the guest without access is named, gets viewer in one step, and the audit entry exists.
Add a guest from a domain that isn't on the POLICY-001 allowlist: the grant is refused with the policy named.
Through the Chat app, share a restricted file into a space with mixed membership.
The card shows no title.
A member with access presses Preview and sees the file; a member without access sees Request access without the title.
The sharer's private prompt names the members without access, and a one-step grant lets them open it.
A subscribed comment notification reaches the space.
Search through the app as two users returns only what each can open.
Repeat the share in the Chat mobile app.
A covered user maps a form with a file-upload question to a restricted folder.
Two respondents each submit a file; each file appears once in the folder with form, response and source Drive file provenance, and neither respondent can open it in Chest.
Replay the response notification and run the sweep: there is no duplicate.
The form's Chest folder links the responses Sheet, which opens under EDIT-002, and no response rows are copied into Chest.
Revoke Meet filing, the Calendar add-on, the Chat app and Forms filing one at a time, then the whole connection.
The next filing, attachment check, share and search are each refused, and files already filed keep their Chest permissions.
Owners preview naming, sorting, tagging, conversion and safe-unzip rules over selected arrivals/folders.
Rules execute idempotently with original bytes, conversion lineage, policy version, item results and an undo plan; changed permissions, unsafe archives or conflicts stop affected items visibly.
Rules cannot broaden sharing, bypass exact-version approval or delete originals.
**Acceptance evidence:** Preview a rename/tag/move/convert/unzip rule over real-format test files, approve it, replay the same event and inspect one result per original.
Submit a traversal/archive bomb and alter a destination grant between preview and execution; retain originals and show blocked items, then undo an untouched move.

Subscriptions and assigned tasks notify through email, Slack, Teams, Google Chat (CONNECT-010) and mobile push for comments, review/change requests, approaching review/expiry dates, file-request deadlines, transfer receipts and unresolved sync failures.
Owners choose US timezone, cadence, escalation recipient and quiet hours; completion, revoked access or canceled work suppresses future reminders.
Job history separates queued, submitted, provider-acknowledged, failed, uncertain and person-confirmed outcomes with authorized retry/reconciliation.
Replying to a comment or mention notification email posts the reply to that thread as the replier.
Each notification has its own signed reply address, and Chest accepts a reply only from the notified address with an aligned SPF or DKIM pass and only while that person still holds commenter access.
Quoted history and signatures are stripped.
A reply from someone who has lost access, from another address, or to a forwarded copy posts nothing, and the sender gets a bounce saying why.
Comment notification emails also carry a **Resolve** action, which opens a signed-in confirmation and applies only while that person can still comment.

Comments, replies, @mentions, assignments and suggestions made inside office files in the EDIT-001 editor are threads like any other: they notify through these channels, and a reply or resolve from the email reaches the comment inside the document as EDIT-001's review loop states.
Comments, mentions and tasks created by a migration batch or delta pass (MIGRATE-001/002) notify no one, and reminders for migrated tasks start one full reminder interval after cutover.

**Personal notification settings:** each person chooses, per channel (email, mobile push, Slack, Teams, Google Chat), which comment notifications they get: all comments on files they own or follow, only mentions, assignments and replies to their comments, or none.
They can mute a file or a thread and switch email to a daily digest at a chosen US time.
Mentions and assignments that arrive while a file is muted still appear in their in-app task list.
Admins with service-settings scope (ADMIN-003) set organization and group defaults, which each person can change for themselves.
**Acceptance evidence:** Assign a dated request and review, subscribe a collaborator, advance a controlled clock through due/reminder/escalation states and complete the exact task.
Fail a provider, restart the worker and inspect the durable result; there is no duplicate reminder or forbidden content after completion/revocation.

Reply by email to a comment notification and see the reply in the thread, attributed and without the quoted history; send the same reply from a different address, and from the original address after their access is revoked, and see neither posted and a bounce returned.
Resolve a comment from its email and see it resolved on the file page.
Mention B in a DOCX comment inside Collabora Online and assign it:
B's email reply appears inside the document, attributed to B, and resolving from B's email resolves it there.

Set one person to "only mentions, assignments and replies" and have them mute a second file: a plain comment on their file sends them nothing, a mention does, and a mention on the muted file sends nothing but appears in their task list.
Switch another person to the daily digest and see one email at their chosen time listing the day's comments.

Migrate an assigned comment under MIGRATE-002 and advance the clock: nothing is sent during the migration, the delta pass or on cutover day, and the first reminder arrives one reminder interval after cutover.
An agent reads granted file contents, OCR/extracted text, email/app provenance and project metadata to propose taxonomy, identify responsible people and file arrivals.
It explains each suggestion with exact-version evidence and uncertainty.
Standing folder grants allow reversible rename/tag/move only; new external access, destructive cleanup and uncertain classification require human approval.
Document instructions are untrusted data and cannot expand tools or scope.

Each filing the agent makes shows as a notice to the people who can see the file, naming the file and its new path (for example "Filed W-9 Acme Supply.pdf → Vendors / Acme / Tax"), with **Undo**, which returns the file to where it arrived with the same stable ID, versions and grants.
The agent's activity view counts the files it filed this week and lists each with its evidence and Undo.
**Acceptance evidence:** Give the agent a project inbox containing ambiguous and malicious-instruction documents, preview its cited classification plan, allow one scoped move and reject another.
Revoke source/destination access before execution; preserve originals and prove the denied/ambiguous action waits without extra reads or messages.

Under a standing folder grant, let the agent file a W-9 that arrived by email (CONNECT-006): the notice names the file and its destination path, Undo returns it to the inbox with the same stable ID and versions, and the activity view's count of files filed this week includes it, listed as undone.

An agent correlates hashes, source IDs, content changes, version history and approvals to find exact/near duplicates and stale copies, propose canonical files and repair authorized internal references.
Equal bytes never imply equal access or identity.
Owners approve merges, overwrites, external link repointing and deletion; reversible consolidation retains originals, old-version references and separate source approvals.
**Acceptance evidence:** Seed duplicate bytes under different ACLs and a near-duplicate with a different signature/date; inspect the proposed version lineage and references.
Approve a safe canonical-link change, reject a merge and verify no access union, lost original or reassigned approval.
An agent correlates device sync queues, hashes, conflict copies, cache health and permission changes to diagnose incomplete files and repair explicitly granted device/folder settings.
It compares both ends before declaring recovery, quarantines uncertain conflicts and requests approval before overwrite, cache deletion or permission expansion.
**Acceptance evidence:** Interrupt a device transfer, create a divergent offline copy and revoke a folder grant.
The agent explains the cause, repairs a permitted paused queue, proves final hashes on both ends and leaves conflict/denied work waiting for the human rather than overwriting or widening access.
For an owner-defined checklist the agent matches request submissions, approvals, transfer receipts and explicit collaborator confirmations to exact requirements/versions.
It identifies missing/superseded evidence, drafts or sends narrowly authorized reminders to approved recipients at the approved cadence, and stops when the correct material is accepted.
A later replacement or permission change reopens the mismatch; views/provider receipts alone do not prove the intended human has the right version.
**Acceptance evidence:** Request two vendor records, receive a stale file and then the correct approved replacement, confirm it as the intended recipient and inspect reminders stopping.
Later revoke access or supersede the version; show the reopened issue and a proposed new delivery, without broadening recipients or auto-approving evidence.
An agent checks current ACLs, guest lifecycle, link policies, intended collaborator lists and actual link outcomes to identify broken, orphaned, stale or excessive shares.
It proposes exact version/audience repairs and explains affected people.
Owners approve new/expanded access and external messages; preauthorized restrictive revocations can run with a reversible record and notification.

Each over-shared item it flags names the link or grant and its audience and offers **Make private**, which, on one click by a person allowed to share the item, removes the broad link or audience and keeps named grants.
It cannot rewrite a vendor-owned URL without control of that source.
**Acceptance evidence:** Create an expired link, departed guest, overshared subfolder and inaccessible approved replacement; run a scan as a restricted agent.
Approve one repair and one restrictive revoke, deny an expansion and confirm destination access and the intended version while unrelated files stay unread.

Flag a public link on a folder that two named staff use: the owner's one Make private click removes the public link, the two staff keep access, and a signed-out browser is refused on the next request.
An agent constructs source-to-Chest identity/folder/version/link mappings using authorized incumbent inventories, reconciles every item/hash/gap and drafts a cutover plan with collaborator journeys.
It can run approved read-only sampling and reversible staging; the owner signs permission mapping, conversion losses, delta boundary and cutover.
It retains source read access and rollback archive until the owner accepts the move.
**Acceptance evidence:** Run against a representative incumbent test tenant with unavailable history, unmapped groups and native files.
Inspect the generated mapping and unresolved gaps, reject an unsafe mapping, approve staging and validate staff/guest open-edit-share workflows before explicitly accepting cutover; exercise rollback.
Users ask questions, extract fields and define bounded custom document agents over expressly granted folders/versions.
Answers cite accessible original passages and extraction provenance, distinguish missing/uncertain evidence and retain the model/tool/data policy used.
Owners select provider, data retention/residency, spend budget and human approval points; tool calls obey the same current ACLs and never autonomously approve/sign/delete or expand permissions.

Questions are also asked where the file is, as Gemini in Drive offers: an **Ask** panel on every file and folder page, in the browser at both widths and in the iOS and Android apps, summarizes the file or folder or answers a question about it.
It uses only files the asker can currently open, cites them, and lists the files a folder summary skipped with the reason (no access, unreadable, not yet extracted).

**Acceptance evidence:** Ask a cross-file question with a contradictory revision and an inaccessible answer-bearing file, inspect exact citations and uncertainty, then run a schema extraction under a small approved budget.
Change access mid-run and inject document tool instructions; deny forbidden retrieval/actions and expose provider failure/cost without fabricated answers or fallback success.

From a folder page at 1440 and 390 and in the iOS and Android apps, ask for a folder summary: it cites only files the asker can open and lists the skipped files with reasons; ask a question from a PDF's file page and see the answer cite its pages.
The owner sets their name at Finish setup; invitations, file requests, notice emails and the audit trail name people by it (by email until a name is set), never by the placeholder "Owner".

The retained real-browser journey uploads 150 MB at 1440/390, interrupts after 26%, reloads, checks the persisted unfinished percentage, rechooses the same file, verifies resumed progress without resending stored parts, and compares both stored and downloaded SHA-256 with the original.
None.
fragments.note: Template leak: an empty-gap marker ("None.") on a done row; done rows now carry an empty Gap.

fragments.text: The repository journey installs genuine v0.1.0 source, bootstraps its owner without mail using the supported installer, and populates it through its original development runtime.

It checks out the candidate in that same installation, runs pinned install/dev and compares every earlier application/auth/import table, schema and row, including the migration ledger, plus every original object hash and metadata.
SQLite/D1 engine bookkeeping is outside application state.
Every retained Library version downloads with its admitted SHA-256, people remain and a team space is created and opened at 1440/390.
Clone/upgrade coverage runs on release tags and nightly, preserving push Verify speed.

Team spaces, personal areas, nested folders with inherited grants and a breadcrumb, create/rename/move/copy/trash, untyped upload by drop, picker or phone camera, stable IDs, restricted subfolders, star, recent, shortcuts and offboarding to a successor exist;

Personal-file and folder ownership offers now require recipient acceptance, preserve IDs, original versions, links and grants, support decline/cancel and optional sender editor access, and notify both parties by email and in-app.

Acceptance hands existing public links and upload requests to the recipient without changing their tokens or original authorship, even if the sender relinquishes direct access; arrivals notify the new custodian.
Changed content, identities or destination collisions cannot silently complete an old offer.
The file page explains current inherited, direct, group and organization-link access.

Delegated organization service-settings admins can set creation formats and publish or unpublish organization and group templates through the browser and API; current scope and source access are required, revocation removes controls and refuses mutations, and publication grants no source access.

The browser New menu creates valid blank Office/OpenDocument files and independent copies from built-in or audience-scoped published templates, with caller-key idempotency, quota admission, creator attribution, search and recent visibility.

Selected folders require exact-version review of new originals, inherited through subfolders and retained on moved files; approved A stays current while B/C await review, and restore, editor saves, sync and file-request arrivals enter as new submissions.
Reviewer assignment grants no access.

Governed folders now select a managed type inherited by subfolders: uploads and creation require valid typed values and an accountable person; schema edits preserve stored values, diagnose only accessible items, and refuse stale replacements/restores.
Resumable uploads retain filing values; corrections are audited.
Moves retain governance and typed values.
Missing: the full EDIT-004 Collabora/provider/native experience and a SCALE-001 reference-size run.
None for ROLE-001.
Commenter DOCX typing is tracked before the first keystroke and every save checks current authority, authorship and unchanged base content.
Contributors decide one engine change per saved version.
PDF regions stay bound to their retained original; restricted previews return raster pages and suppress copy and printing.
Built-in suggestions retain their single pending batch limit.
EDIT-001 and EDIT-003 retain the broader shared engine thread, task, notification and email loop, other format and native acceptance;
EDIT-002 and MIGRATE-002 through MIGRATE-006 retain imported-review fidelity.
None.
Chest hosts the configured Collabora editor in a frame and checks for a new restore every 12 seconds with the editor token and current file authority.
Only messages from that frame at the configured editor origin are accepted.
The host sends the Collabora version-restore handshake; the engine saves, closes and reloads its document.
Chest never discards the frame on a timer, and a pending reconciliation keeps the editor and its unsaved work available while stale writes remain refused.
This proves the VERSION-001 restore door without claiming EDIT-001's broader review, packaging, provider or native acceptance.
MIGRATE-002 through MIGRATE-006 inherit migration provenance;

Broader target behavior stays in the target clauses below.
The target makes Chest responsible for the file-system job, native clients, sync, external exchange, search, integration experience and recovery.

Under that target, native filesystem drivers run in maintained signed macOS/Windows clients; heavy OCR, rendering, media conversion and malware scanning, and the shipped Collabora Online editor (EDIT-001), run in separately deployed bounded services.

Worker limits are an engineering deployment boundary, not a reason to omit these capabilities (SYNC-001/004, PREVIEW-001, SEARCH-001, SECURITY-002). iOS/Android distribution, OS entitlements, provider app registrations, API scopes, licensing, agreements and real-account acceptance are delivery work in the named clauses.

The EDIT-001/002 target integrates Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and Collabora Online editing engines rather than building another office suite; it requires Chest to ship and deploy Collabora Online as its default editor, so co-authoring needs no Microsoft or Google license (EDIT-001).
CAD/video/design creation remains in Adobe Creative Cloud, AutoCAD and Final Cut Pro, supported through SYNC-004.
Salesforce and HubSpot own CRM;
Slack, Teams and Google Chat own chat;
Zoom and Google Meet own meetings;
Google Calendar and Outlook own scheduling.
Chest is the file store behind each of them: their recordings, attachments and shared files land in and link to Chest (CONNECT-001–003, CONNECT-005, CONNECT-008 and CONNECT-010).
Other vendors' "attach from Google Drive" pickers belong to those vendors;
Chest offers them the CONNECT-007 embeddable picker and API, the CONNECT-009 automation apps and the SYNC-001 mount, and does not claim a picker inside a product until that vendor ships one.
The SIGN-001 target requires Chest to execute everyday ESIGN/UETA signatures itself, as Google Workspace does;
Docusign remains an integration for firms that standardize on it and for remote online notarization and EU qualified signatures (CONNECT-004).
Chest keeps their files, pointers, version provenance and custody synchronized through CONNECT-001–007.
It does not merge those products or absorb unassigned categories.
Legal hold, certified regulated custody and discovery require a qualified provider and verified policy under GOVERN-001, not a marketing claim about generic object storage.
Any BAA or regulated-data provider agreement needed for a buyer is acceptance work before that workload is enabled, not permission to remove the capability.
The first buyer operates in the United States.

Commercial costs and estimates are USD, dates are unambiguous, stored times retain UTC plus the selected US business time zone, and guest collection/signature flows support US business counterparties.
Chest does not replace payroll (Envelope, sibling seed), tax, accounting or payment products; it stores their files and integrates authorized sources.
No unmeasured price, storage capacity, throughput, vendor fidelity, accessibility certification or compliance outcome is claimed.

Today, searchable extraction covers UTF-8 text up to 500 kB, native RTF displayed text, PDF text layers, Office and OpenDocument text, and OCR of scans and photos with the installation's own AI model key (up to 60 scanned pages and 900,000 characters per file); originals sent through the plain upload form or the JSON API have an 8 MB admission limit and resumable uploads take up to 4 GB per file; reviewed JSON move-in archives have 100-item/16 MB bounds.
Current PDF and raster viewing uses the browser, and DOCX/XLSX/PPTX have built-in previews.
Search also combines the named type, people, date, location and version filters and finds matches in earlier versions, labeled with their exact version.
These are delivered subsets of TRANSFER-001, PREVIEW-001 and SEARCH-001; their larger limits, complete format matrices, native-app search and the SCALE-001 search target remain required.

The current implementation also includes five-level space roles, space-creation control and new-space defaults (SPACE-002), self-service trash and restore (CHEST-13), staff version operations with the VERSION-001 gaps below, multi-select bulk actions and ZIP64 archive download in the browser (BULK-001), folder/space/personal-area rewind (RECOVER-001), scheduled independent backups and upgrade recovery (RECOVER-002), item sharing and access requests (SHARE-004), public, organization, named-guest and exact-domain reader links, the organization, space and creator-group sharing policy (POLICY-001), upload-only file requests (SHARE-002), delivery receipts and large-file transfers (SHARE-003), storage limits (QUOTA-001), browser creation from blank or templates, built-in DOCX text/XLSX value editing, version-bound comments, typed fields read from scans on Library records and in typed folders (SEARCH-002), identity federation and provisioning (ADMIN-001), several super admins, delegated admin roles, owner transfer and scoped account rewind (ADMIN-003), native multi-factor sign-in (ADMIN-004), browser and device-protocol upload protection that pauses suspect replacements (SECURITY-003), durable searchable/exportable audit history (AUDIT-001), deliberate erasure (ERASE-001), the MIT release with its complete production license inventory (OPEN-001), OAuth apps, MCP, webhooks, the embeddable picker and third-party app control (CONNECT-007), Cloudflare email intake, reversible arrival filing (RULE-001), AI filing of authorized arrivals (AGENT-001), duplicate consolidation with Undo (AGENT-002), a sync-repair companion (AGENT-003), exact-version collection (AGENT-004), and link exposure warnings and repairs with Make private (AGENT-005), and built-in eSignature in the browser with PIN-verified signers, a PAdES seal and an audit certificate (SIGN-001).
